chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: Email My Office Call My Office: 305-222-0160 Carlos Antonio Gimenez proudly represents the people of Florida’s 28th congressional district, encompassing all of Monroe County and the southwest portion of Miami-Dade County. Congressman Carlos Giménez was first elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2020, becoming the only current Cuban-born member of Congress and the first career firefighter-paramedic to serve in Congress.

chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: He currently serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Homeland Security Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Transportation and Maritime Security. Appointed by the Speaker of the House, he is also a member of the House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and he serves on the Board of Regents for the Smithsonian Institution and the Mexico–United States Interparliamentary Group. Within Republican leadership, Rep. Giménez serves as Vice Chairman of the Republican Governance Group (RG2) and Vice Chair of Community Outreach for the Congressional Hispanic Conference.

chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: Carlos is a husband, father, grandfather, and a public servant who has dedicated his life to serving the Miami-Dade community. Born in 1954, Carlos arrived to the United States shortly after the Communist takeover of his native homeland of Cuba, settling in the Little Havana neighborhood in Miami. His family’s experience helped shape his servant’s heart and his dedication to this community, understanding the importance of protecting individuals’ freedom to pursue their potential.

chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: Carlos began his journey of public service in 1975 when he joined the City of Miami Fire Department. There, he embarked on a 25-year career as a firefighter in his community, with the last nine years of his tenure as Chief of the department - the very first Cuban American to serve as the Chief of the City of Miami Fire Department. Congressman Gimenez is married to his wife Lourdes. They have three adult children – Carlos, Julio, and Lourdes – and six grandchildren.

chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: In 2000, Carlos was appointed Manager of the City of Miami, overseeing a $500 million annual budget and nearly 4,000 city government employees, with the goal of implementing critical fiscal and administrative reforms for the sustainability of City of Miami operations.

chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: In this capacity, Carlos reduced the city’s tax rate to the lowest level in 50 years while generating more revenue for the city. Four years later, Carlos was elected as Miami-Dade County Commissioner where he served the county’s 7th district until 2011. In the summer of 2011, Carlos was elected as Mayor of Miami-Dade County, the highest-ranking official of Florida’s largest county.

chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: He maintained his commitment to bringing fiscal responsibility needed at the county level, working to expand transparency, renegotiate contracts with public sector labor unions and reduce the county government workforce, and implementing the largest tax cut in the county’s history saving Miami-Dade County taxpayers $2 billion. He was subsequently re-elected as Mayor in 2012 and again in 2016.

chunks.title: About | Representative Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: Carlos is a proud graduate from Christopher Columbus High School in Westchester, FL and earned a bachelor’s degree in Public Administration from Barry University in Miami, FL. He completed the Program for Senior Executives in State and Local Government at Harvard University’s John F. Kennedy School of Government.

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez Resources for American Citizens in Israel CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Carlos Gimenez (R-FL) re-introduced the Miccosukee Reserved Area Amendments Act . This bill will incorporate the Osceola Camp into the Miccosukee Reserved Area (MRA). Incorporation of the Osceola Camp will improve the facilities and governing structure of the Tribe. Further, these changes will optimize water flow into Everglades National Park while keeping residence Osceola Camp unaffected.

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: This legislation is supported by the Miccosukee Tribe. " As the Representative for the Miccosukee Tribe, I have seen firsthand the Tribe's dedication to being outstanding stewards of the Everglades, as well as their role as a vital community partner, fostering jobs and opportunities for South Floridians ," said Congressman Carlos Gimenez . " I am eager to continue collaborating with the Tribe to protect our cherished River of Grass and integrate the Osceola Camp into the Miccosukee Reserved Area. "

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: “ The Miccosukee Tribe has called the Everglades home for centuries and have been critical partners in protecting the environment ,” said Congresswoman Maria Salazar . “ This bill, which incorporates the Osceola Camp into the Miccosukee Reserved Area (MRA), further recognizes the Tribe’s connection to this land and allows them to have a significant role in protecting it from flooding. I am proud to cosponsor this legislation and I encourage my colleagues to join in support as well. ”

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: “ As a staunch supporter of our Native American tribes, I recognize the challenges faced by the Miccosukee Tribe, particularly with the Osceola Camp, which has been severely impacted by flooding following recent tropical storms. I am proud to join my South Florida colleagues in introducing this critical legislation, which aims to remove current mitigation barriers placed on the Tribe by the federal government and enhance communication with the Department of Interior. These joint efforts will ensure that we take appropriate actions in protecting the structures within the Osceola Camp, ” said Congressman Mario Díaz-Balart.

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: Senator Rick Scott said, “ The Miccosukee Tribe’s Osceola Camp has been a home and site of cultural significance for generations of Tribal members and I am proud to introduce this bill with my colleagues to ensure its protection. I deeply appreciate the partnership I have had with the Miccosukee Tribe as Florida Governor, and will continue to support their interests as U.S. Senator. ”

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: “ The passage of the Miccosukee Reserve Area Act Amendment is an important step forward to facilitate the continued practice of Miccosukee traditions at the Osceola Tribal Camp in advance of increased water levels into the Shark River Slough and Everglades National Park ," said Miccosukee Tribe Chairman Talbert Cypress . “ As Everglades Restoration continues, our partners in Congress like Representatives Carlos Gimenez, Mario Diaz-Balart, and Elvia Maria Salazar, and Senator Rick Scott, continue to fulfill Congress’s trust obligations to the Miccosukee Tribe on balance with the important work of the Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan.

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN CARLOS GIMENEZ INTRODUCES BILL TO INCORPORATE OSCEOLA CAMP INTO THE MRA | Press Releases | Congressman Carlos Gimenez
chunks.text: This small expansion of tribal sovereignty will allow our Tribe to maintain its traditional footprint and empower the Tribe to raise the Osceola Camp to prevent flooding. We thank Congress for their swift and thoughtful action to assist the Miccosukee Tribe and its members. ”

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN GIMENEZ INTRODUCES THE PRESERVING OPTIONS FOR EVERGLADES RESTORATION AND NATIONAL DEFENSE IN THE STRAITS OF FLORIDA ACT | Press Releases |
chunks.text: MIAMI, FL - Congressman Carlos Gimenez (FL-28) introduced the Preserving Options for Everglades Restoration and National Defense in the Straits of Florida Act , which would extend the prohibition on the joint use of Homestead Air Reserve Base by the Air Force and civil aircraft. Last year, the prohibition was included in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA).

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN GIMENEZ INTRODUCES THE PRESERVING OPTIONS FOR EVERGLADES RESTORATION AND NATIONAL DEFENSE IN THE STRAITS OF FLORIDA ACT | Press Releases |
chunks.text: “ Preserving the Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB) for its original intent and purpose is critical to protecting our national security interests ,” Gimenez said . “ Allowing aircraft not affiliated with our military or armed services to utilize an air reserve facility would only compromise our country's national security. Extending the prohibiting the joint use of the Homestead Air Reserve Base ensures the protection of our strategic interests and protects the precious South Florida ecosystem caught in between Biscayne National Park and Everglades National Park. ”

chunks.title: CONGRESSMAN GIMENEZ INTRODUCES THE PRESERVING OPTIONS FOR EVERGLADES RESTORATION AND NATIONAL DEFENSE IN THE STRAITS OF FLORIDA ACT | Press Releases |
chunks.text: For years, Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB) has been a central focus of special interests that wish to secure commercial passenger and cargo operations to expand the urban development boundary in southern Miami-Dade County. Those proposals have the potential to impact military readiness and diminish efforts to conserve and restore critical habitat near HARB and Biscayne Bay. The Preserving Options for Everglades Restoration and National Defense in the Straits of Florida Act guarantees the protection of our South Dade ecosystem and ensures that Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB) will continue to operate for its original intended purpose.

chunks.title: About - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Ashley Moody was sworn into the United States Senate on January 21, 2025, after being appointed by Governor Ron DeSantis. Ashley Moody is a fifth-generation Floridian, born and raised in Plant City, Florida. She attended the University of Florida, where she earned both her bachelor’s and master’s degrees in accounting, as well as her law degree. Additionally, she obtained a Master of Laws in International Law from Stetson University College of Law.

chunks.title: About - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Moody began her career at the law firm Holland & Knight, where she practiced commercial litigation. In her spare time, she volunteered to assist domestic violence victims seeking protection in court. She later joined the United States Attorney’s Office, where she prosecuted drug, firearm, and fraud offenses. In 2006, at the age of thirty-one, Senator Moody became the youngest judge in Florida when she was elected as Circuit Court Judge of the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit in Hillsborough County.

chunks.title: About - Senator Moody
chunks.text: From 2019 to 2025, Senator Moody served as Florida’s 38th Attorney General. During her tenure, she was recognized as a national leader and served as a Commissioner on the Presidential Commission on Law Enforcement and the Administration of Justice during the first Trump administration.

chunks.title: About - Senator Moody
chunks.text: She also chaired Florida’s Statewide Council on Human Trafficking, led efforts against the harmful open-border policies of the Biden administration, supported and recruited law enforcement officers to protect Floridians, worked to defend children against invasive and addictive Big Tech policies, fought Big Pharma and was awarded billions of dollars for Florida through historic opioid litigation and protected Florida consumers against deceptive trade practices. As a United States Senator, Moody is focused on supporting President Trump’s agenda, securing the border, standing up for the rule of law, and continuing her work to ensure that Florida remains safe and prosperous for years to come.

chunks.title: Storm Preparation - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Every natural disaster or emergency provides an opportunity for unscrupulous individuals to try to take advantage of the crisis and prey on those in distress. chunks.title: Sens. Ashley Moody and Rick Scott Introduce Bill to Provide Tax Relief for Skyrocketing Flood Insurance Costs - Senator Moody
chunks.text: WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senators Ashley Moody and Rick Scott introduced the Flood Insurance Relief Act to provide tax relief for Americans with a non-refundable tax deduction on flood insurance premiums paid through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or through private insurers. This bill will help ease the financial burden of rising flood insurance costs for hardworking Americans in Florida and across the nation. Congressman Byron Donalds is leading the companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

chunks.title: Sens. Ashley Moody and Rick Scott Introduce Bill to Provide Tax Relief for Skyrocketing Flood Insurance Costs - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Ashley Moody said, “As I travel around the Sunshine State, one thing folks continue to tell me is that they are worried about the rising cost of flood insurance. That is why today, Senator Scott and I are working to ease the financial burden on Florida families by proposing a bill that would create a tax deduction on their flood insurance premiums. The Flood Insurance Relief Act is a critical solution that will directly benefit Floridians.”

chunks.title: Sens. Ashley Moody and Rick Scott Introduce Bill to Provide Tax Relief for Skyrocketing Flood Insurance Costs - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Rick Scott said, “Floridians know well that flood insurance can be a crucial but costly asset, and it is unacceptable that many are left struggling to find flood insurance coverage they can afford. Families shouldn’t have to choose between protecting their homes and putting food on the table. I’ve been working on several bills to fix the broken NFIP system and encourage private-sector participation to allow for a more robust, affordable flood insurance market, but we must do more to help families ASAP.

chunks.title: Sens. Ashley Moody and Rick Scott Introduce Bill to Provide Tax Relief for Skyrocketing Flood Insurance Costs - Senator Moody
chunks.text: My Flood Insurance Relief Act offers a practical way to directly ease the financial burden of flood insurance for families by allowing a tax deduction on their premiums, whether through the NFIP or the private market. I’m glad to have my fellow Floridians Senator Ashley Moody and Congressman Byron Donalds joining me in leading this effort.”

chunks.title: Sens. Ashley Moody and Rick Scott Introduce Bill to Provide Tax Relief for Skyrocketing Flood Insurance Costs - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Congressman Byron Donalds said, “For far too long, the rising cost of flood insurance has crushed hardworking Floridians. This is unacceptable, this must change, and this critical issue must be addressed to ensure our economy works for all Americans. The time for action is now, and I’m proud to join Senator Rick Scott in introducing the Flood Insurance Relief Act to provide this overdue relief to policyholders across our Southwest Florida community, the Sunshine State, and the nation.”

chunks.text: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures More than $2.3 BILLION for Florida Communities Affected by Disasters - Senator Moody VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures More than $2.3 BILLION for Florida Communities Affected by Disasters FORT MYERS BEACH, Fla.— Senator Ashley Moody continues working to secure long-sought FEMA disaster funds for hard-hit Florida communities. Since taking office, Senator Moody has recovered more than $2.3 billion for Florida. Senator Moody stood with local emergency officials in Fort Myers Beach to break the news today on the peak day of hurricane season. Included in the $2.3 billion secured for statewide projects are more than $64.9 million for projects in Lee County.

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures More than $2.3 BILLION for Florida Communities Affected by Disasters - Senator Moody
chunks.text: “When I got to Washington, Florida was still owed billions of dollars for projects dating back years. We quickly went to work to cut through the bureaucracy and make sure our communities received the money they were owed. Today, we announced that our total recoveries have officially surpassed $2 billion. This is a major milestone, but our work isn’t over yet. We will keep working to deliver the federal support Floridians need,” said Senator Ashley Moody .

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures More than $2.3 BILLION for Florida Communities Affected by Disasters - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Statewide, Senator Moody has secured more than $2.3 billion in FEMA public assistance funding. Included in these funds are more than $64.9 million secured for Lee County, with $5.5. million designated to help reconstruct the pier destroyed by Hurricane Ian. The replacement is planned to stretch roughly 1,000 feet into the Gulf, more than 70% longer than the one destroyed. These grants will be distributed along with the previously announced funds through FEMA’s Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation Assistance programs to support more than 500 recovery projects across the state. This money is disbursed to the state and local communities for disaster recovery projects.

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Senator Moody Touts $1.5 Billion in Secured FEMA Reimbursements for Florida and Passage of Her TRACK Act as Hurricane Season Looms - Se
chunks.text: “As hurricane season approaches, our work to help Floridians recover from storms or other natural disasters continues. I’m proud to have secured more than $1.5 billion in long-overdue FEMA funding to support communities across our state, while also advancing solutions like the TRACK Act to bring greater transparency to the recovery process,” said Senator Ashley Moody. chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Senator Moody Touts $1.5 Billion in Secured FEMA Reimbursements for Florida and Passage of Her TRACK Act as Hurricane Season Looms - Se
chunks.text: Senator Moody introduced the  TRACK Act  (Transparency in Recovery Assistance & Claims Knowledge Act) to bring more transparency to the FEMA disaster aid process and has now passed into law. The TRACK Bill mandates a status tracker on the FEMA website, so victims of a disaster have easily available knowledge and insight of their claim’s progress. Senator Moody is also urging Floridians ahead of the start of this year’s hurricane season to be ready to weather any storm: Build an emergency supply kit, with enough bottled water, nonperishable food, medications, and pet supplies to last at least seven days; Stay informed about potential storm threats by listening to local officials;

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Senator Moody Touts $1.5 Billion in Secured FEMA Reimbursements for Florida and Passage of Her TRACK Act as Hurricane Season Looms - Se
chunks.text: Create a family safety plan that outlines what you will do and where you will go in the event of a hurricane strike; and Reduce home hazards by placing large, heavy objects on lower shelves and removing objects from your yard that could become projectiles. To view Senator Moody’s full remarks at today’s event, click  here .

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate Hardworking people should get to determine and shape what their communities look like and what their economies look like. – Alphonso Mayfield (Labor Leader and Fighter for all Floridians) A Government that Works for its People, Not Corporations Angie believes that the government should work for working people — not corporations, not billionaires, and not the political establishment in either party that keeps letting them win. Ask any Florida family what’s on their mind — whether they’re a Democrat, Republican, or don’t care much for either party — and you’ll hear the same thing: everything costs too much, and their paycheck can’t keep up.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Since the pandemic, household expenses have jumped nearly a third. In Florida, the cost of living is climbing almost five times faster than it did a decade ago. Meanwhile, wages have stayed the same. Today, only a third of Floridians think our own state is affordable.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: This isn’t an accident. It isn’t inevitable. While the average American is struggling, corporate landlords, insurance companies, and grocery chains have posted record profits. This year, Elon Musk became the world’s first trillionaire. And instead of delivering relief, politicians in Washington have spent months absorbed in a war that’s driving gas and energy prices even higher, while killing innocent civilians and American service people. Enough is enough. Angie will fight for the Working Families Guarantee A National Rent Freeze and Moratorium on Evictions A universal jobs program with inflation-adjusted wages Tax the billionaires so that everyone pays their fair share

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Prioritize the needs of everyday Americans instead of spending trillions on war and violence overseas Foreign Policy rooted in Human Rights & Restraint Climate Action Matching the Scale of the Crisis The United States is the richest country on earth but doesn’t guarantee healthcare to all its people. Americans pay more for worse outcomes than anywhere else in the developed world. That’s not a healthcare system, it’s a protection racket for insurance and drug companies.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Roughly 100 million Americans — about 4 in 10 adults — carry some form of medical debt, totaling at least $220 billion nationwide. People aren’t going into debt because they made bad choices; they’re going into debt because they got sick, had a baby or broke a bone. Medicare for All  that covers every person in America — free at the point of service, with no premiums, no deductibles, no copays, and no surprise bills. Comprehensive coverage , including dental, vision, hearing, mental health and substance use treatment, reproductive and maternity care, and prescription drugs. Capping prescription drug costs  and ending price gouging by drug companies.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Protecting reproductive freedom , including the right to abortion, contraception, and IVF, free from political interference. Expanding home and community-based long-term care  so seniors and people with disabilities can age with dignity. Canceling the medical debt crushing families.  Canceling existing medical debt, wiping it off credit reports for good, and banning debt collectors from coming after patients for medical bill. Angie support senator Sanders’ bipartisan-backed Medical Debt Cancellation Act. Paid family and medical leave  for every worker in America, guaranteed by law Angie believes in Universal Child Care & Pre-K.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Child care in America costs more than college tuition in most states. As a mom of 5, Angie knows this struggle deeply because she is experiencing it. Universal, high-quality child care and pre-kindergarten  for every family, regardless of income, capping costs so no family pays more than a small share of their income. Living wages for child care and early-childhood educators , who are among the most underpaid workers in the country despite doing some of its most important work. Universal school meals  so no child goes hungry during the school day. Angie believes in quality Public Education.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Getting an education in America shouldn’t mean a lifetime of debt. About 43 million Americans now owe nearly $2 trillion in student loan debt. That’s about $43,500 per borrower, meaning people owe more for simply trying to get an education than they do on their cars or credit cards.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: A degree that was once a ticket to the middle class has become a financial trap for millions of families, forcing young people to delay buying a home, starting a family, or saving for retirement just to keep up with payments on an education they were told they needed to get ahead. It’s not a personal failure; it’s the predictable result of a system that treats higher education as a private commodity instead of a public good. Tuition-free public college and trade school , and canceling student debt. Fully funding public K-12 schools   and increased teacher wages Expanding vocational and apprenticeship programs  that lead directly to good union jobs.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Angie believes in housing you can actually afford. Rent is too high, homeownership is out of reach for millions, and Wall Street landlords are buying up housing stock and squeezing renters to enrich themselves. Florida is getting hit the hardest, and is now the worst state in the country for renters. On top of this, Florida homeowners now pay some of the highest insurance premiums in the nation — often as high as $10,000 a year — nearly three to four times the national average. Housing is a human right, not a speculative asset for the billionaire class. Massive investment in permanently affordable housing , building millions of new affordable units nationwide.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: A national rent stabilization standard , just-cause eviction protections, and the right to counsel in eviction proceedings. Cracking down on corporate landlords and Wallstreet speculators  buying up single-family homes and driving up rents. Expanding Section 8 vouchers  so every eligible family can access one without languishing on a waitlist. Federal action on the property insurance crisis , including reinsurance backstops and stronger consumer protections, so Floridians aren’t priced out of their own homes by an insurance market that keeps failing them. Disaster resilience funding  to harden homes against hurricanes Angie believes in standing with workers & unions.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: For too long, corporations have rigged labor law against working people. Angie was a labor organizer and will fight for the dignity of all workers. Passing the PRO Act  to make it easier to form a union and harder for corporations to bust one. Paid family and medical leave  for every worker in America, guaranteed by law. Raising the federal minimum wage  to a real living wage, indexed to inflation, for every worker, including immigrant and incarcerated workers. Ending “right to work” laws  and extending labor protections to workers historically excluded from them, including farmworkers and domestic workers.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Protecting pensions and Social Security , and expanding benefits rather than cutting them. Fighting outsourcing  and trade policy that has hollowed out American manufacturing towns Angie believes in reining in big tech & AI companies. AI companies are racing to build massive data centers, and everyday families are getting stuck with the bill through higher electricity rates, strained water supplies and job cuts — while a handful of billionaires reap the profits.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: On top of this, AI companies are rushing products to market that millions now use every day — — with little to no safety testing and no accountability when things go wrong. And things have gone wrong: families have testified before Congress after AI chatbots encouraged self-harm, failed to intervene during a mental health crisis, or in the most tragic cases, were linked to a child’s suicide. This isn’t a hypothetical harm. It’s already happened, and the companies that built these products have moved faster than the laws meant to hold them accountable. Making tech companies pay for the energy and water they use , not passing those costs on to ratepayers.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: No new construction of data centers before there are real federal guardrails put in place , including environmental review and community input requirements. Protecting workers from AI-driven job displacement , including a real seat at the table for workers and unions as automation reshapes their industries. Breaking up concentrated tech monopolies  and strengthening antitrust enforcement against Big Tech. Protecting personal data privacy  and preventing AI-driven surveillance and discrimination.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Real safety requirements for AI chatbots and companion apps , including mandatory protocols to detect suicidal ideation and connect users to real crisis resources — not silence, and not an AI pretending to be a therapist. Clear disclosure that a user is talking to a machine, not a person  — at the start of every conversation and repeated regularly, so no one, especially a child, is confused or manipulated into an unhealthy emotional dependency. Banning AI companies from letting chatbots impersonate licensed doctors, therapists, or attorneys Independent safety testing before AI products reach kids , not after the harm is already done.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Funding for families and survivors  to pursue accountability, and support for the crisis-response infrastructure (like 988) that these products should be routing kids toward, not away from. Angie believes in a foreign policy rooted in diplomacy, human rights, and restraint. Angie believes American foreign policy should reflect the values of everyday Americans, not the interests of billionaire defense contractors. This year, lawmakers signed a $1.01 trillion defense budget while Americans at home struggle to afford housing and healthcare. End to the war in Iran and rebalance the federal budget toward investments in everyday people here at home

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Uphold international law and institutions. Angie believes we should use the UN and multilateral diplomacy, not unilateral military action, as the first tool for resolving international conflicts, including in the Middle East. Build a future of lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis in the region rooted in safety, equality and democracy for all people and respect for international law and human rights. This includes an end to US support for illegal settlements in the West Bank and upholding the ceasefire agreement in Gaza. Surge aid to places facing humanitarian crises such as: Gaza, the Westbank, Lebanon, Yemen, the Congo and Sudan

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Uphold US law, including the The Leahy Law, which states U.S. taxpayer dollars and military assistance can never be used to enable violations of human rights, regardless of which country receives that aid. Restore U.S. participation and funding across UN agencies and public health programs that Americans and the rest of the world rely on. Restore humanitarian funding, including support that helps deliver food, medicine, and aid to refugees and children in crisis zones around the world. Angie believes in supporting human dignity, ending mass incarceration and deportation.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: The US has the largest policing, incarceration and deportation system in the world. Millions of people — disproportionately Black, brown, and poor — are locked in cages or living in fear of a knock on the door, while corporations get rich off their suffering. This is not about safety. It is about control and profit. I don’t believe any person is illegal, and I don’t believe human beings should be treated as commodities in a system built to punish rather than to heal. Real safety comes from good jobs, strong schools, affordable housing, and healthcare for all — not from more cameras, more cages, and more agents tearing families apart.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: It is time we had the courage to say it plainly: mass incarceration and mass deportation are moral failures, and I will fight in the United States Senate to end them. Ending mass incarceration , including federal decriminalization of marijuana and investment in treatment over incarceration for substance use. Demilitarizing policing  and investing in community-based public safety, violence prevention and crisis response A humane immigration system , including a swift path to citizenship for Dreamers and undocumented residents, and a moratorium on deportations pending a full audit of enforcement practices.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Abolishing ICE and rebuilding immigration enforcement from scratch.  Since its creation in 2003, ICE has operated with almost no accountability — and that’s escalated into real tragedy, including U.S. citizens killed by federal immigration agents during enforcement surges in cities like Minneapolis. Angie believes an agency that has repeatedly shown it cannot be trusted with the power it has should not be reformed at the margins — it should be dismantled, with any legitimate immigration enforcement function rebuilt under new, accountable civilian oversight, due process protections, and a mission that reflects American values instead of terror tactics.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Across the country, communities are pushing back against the rapid, unregulated spread of AI-powered surveillance technology — including automated license plate readers (ALPRs) like those sold by Flock Safety. These systems can track every vehicle that passes a camera, building a searchable record of where people go, when, and how often. That data can end up in the hands of federal immigration agents, out-of-state law enforcement, or bad actors — often without a warrant, without public knowledge, and without meaningful oversight. I believe you shouldn’t have to choose between public safety and your right to privacy.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Requiring warrants for Surveillance Data Access. Law enforcement should not be able to search months of a person’s movements without judicial oversight. I will fight for federal standards requiring a warrant before ALPR or similar location data can be accessed in most circumstances. Ending Data Sharing with Federal Immigration Enforcement. Local police departments should not become a surveillance arm of ICE or CBP. I support legislation prohibiting the sharing of license plate and location data with federal immigration authorities absent a criminal warrant.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Mandatory Data Deletion Windows. Indefinite retention of everyone’s movements — regardless of suspicion — is not acceptable. I will push for federal guidelines requiring surveillance data to be deleted within a short, defined window (in line with state laws that already require deletion within weeks) unless it is tied to an active investigation. Transparency and Public Accountability. Communities deserve to know when surveillance systems are installed, who has access to the data, how it’s used, and how often it leads to shared information with outside agencies. I support requiring public reporting and independent audits for any federally funded surveillance program.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Ending Federal Funding for Mass Surveillance Systems Without Guardrails. Taxpayer dollars should not underwrite surveillance systems that lack basic privacy protections. I will advocate for tying federal grants and infrastructure funding to clear limits on ALPR use, data sharing, and retention. Protect Vulnerable Communities from Targeting. Surveillance systems have a documented history of disproportionately impacting immigrants, communities of color, and political dissidents. Any federal framework must include explicit protections against discriminatory use and misuse for political or retaliatory purposes.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Local Control and Consent. Decisions about whether to deploy surveillance technology in a community should involve real public input — not be made unilaterally by a mayor’s office or a single department. I support requiring community consent processes before new surveillance contracts are signed or renewed with federal support. Angie believes in climate action that matches the scale of the crisis. The climate crisis is an existential threat, and the fossil fuel industry has spent decades lying about it while cashing in. Angie rejects the false choice between good jobs and a livable planet.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: A bold, union-built transition to renewable energy , creating millions of good-paying, union jobs in wind, solar, and grid modernization, prioritizing the frontline communities that have borne the brunt of pollution for generations. Ending taxpayer subsidies for fossil fuel corporations  and making polluters pay for the damage they’ve caused. Rebuilding and hardening the electric grid , so it’s resilient, affordable, and ready for a clean-energy future Disaster resilience funding  to harden homes against hurricanes. Taking FEMA out of the Department of Homeland Security Angie believes in protecting and expanding democracy, and getting money out of politics.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: When a handful of billionaires can spend hundreds of millions of dollars to influence an election and the average person gets one vote, that’s not a democracy for the many, but a corrupt government working for a few. Angie will fight to make this country a real democracy, so that this government works for all of us, not just the wealthy elite Overturning Citizens United  so corporations and billionaires can no longer buy elections with unlimited, often secret spending.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Abolishing super PACs  and imposing real contribution limits. I suppor the  Abolish Super PACs Act  which would cap super PAC contributions at $5,000 — replacing today’s unlimited-money free-for-all with public financing that amplifies small-dollar donors instead of billionaire donors. Restoring and expanding the Voting Rights Act , including automatic voter registration for every American over 18, and ending racist voter suppression and burdensome voter ID laws. Ending partisan gerrymandering  with independent redistricting commissions. Making Election Day a national holiday , so working people don’t have to choose between their paycheck and their vote.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Re-enfranchising Americans with felony convictions , restoring voting rights to the millions of Americans who have served their time and deserve to have their voice back. Public financing of elections , so candidates can run competitive campaigns without relying on corporate donors. Banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks  while in office. Closing the revolving door  between Congress, federal agencies, and the corporate lobbyists who work to influence them. Full transparency in campaign spending , ending dark money in our elections. Term limits and ethics reform for the Supreme Court , including binding ethics rules for all federal judges.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Statehood for Washington, D.C. , so its residents finally get full representation in Congress. A real, binding process for Puerto Rico to determine its own political future  — statehood, independence, free association, or another path — decided by the people of Puerto Rico themselves, not dictated by Washington. More than 3 million American citizens on the island currently have no vote for president and no voting representation in Congress, despite paying certain federal taxes and serving in the U.S. military at high rates. Angie believes in making billionaires and corporations pay their fair share.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Billionaire fortunes have exploded over the past few years while working families fall further behind on rent, groceries, and medical bills. Florida is home to more billionaires than almost any other state and meanwhile, everyday Floridians are struggling more than anyone with housing costs, healthcare cuts, job loss and inflation. Angie believes we can afford Medicare for All, universal child care, and a clean-energy future. What we can’t afford is letting the richest people in the country keep paying less in taxes than a nurse or a line cook.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: A 5% annual wealth tax on billionaires.  I support Senator Sanders’  Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act , which would apply only to net worth above $1 billion — hitting fewer than 1,000 people in the entire country. Independent economists estimate it would raise roughly $4.4 trillion over ten years without raising taxes by a single dollar on anyone worth less than $1 billion. Direct relief for working families , funded by that revenue — including direct payments to households earning under $150,000 a year, expanding Medicare to cover dental, vision, and hearing, and building millions of affordable homes.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Taxing capital gains the same as wages , so a billionaire’s stock portfolio isn’t taxed at a lower rate than a worker’s paycheck. Closing the loopholes that let profitable corporations pay $0 in federal income tax , including offshore tax havens and the “stepped-up basis” loophole that lets fortunes pass tax-free from one generation to the next. A federal asset registry and real IRS enforcement , so the ultra-wealthy can no longer hide assets or dodge audits — while ensuring the IRS stays focused on high-dollar evasion, not everyday taxpayers.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Cracking down on corporate price gouging  in groceries, housing, and health care, where record corporate profits have tracked closely with what families are paying at the register. Angie believes in combatting anti-blackness, anti-semitism, Islamophobia, Nativism, transphobia, and all forms of hate.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Hatred rooted in identity — whether directed at someone’s religion, race, gender or immigration status — has no place in American life. But hate is not a single, undifferentiated force. It takes distinct historical shapes and requires leaders who understand those differences. As a candidate for the United States Senate, I am committed to fighting antisemitism, Islamophobia, anti-immigrant hate, anti-Black racism and all forms of discrimination with the specificity and seriousness each demands, and to standing against hate crimes of every kind.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Throughout history, the tools of division have shifted targets but repeated their logic – from the pogroms and killing of 6M Jewish people during the Holocaust to the Trans Atlantic Slave trade and Jim crow to the surveillence of Muslim and Arab communities after 9/11 to the violent attacks happening against immigrants in this country today. In each of these instances, the rich and powerful have worked to turn us against each other—so that instead of uniting around an agenda that guarantees everyone the chance at a healthy, thriving life, we’re left blaming our neighbors for problems they didn’t cause.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: But we have far more in common with our neighbors — whatever their faith or background — than we do with the people counting on our division to keep their power intact. My campaign is committed to bringing all people together – across race, religion, geography and partisanship – to build a Florida where the safety, freedom and dignity of all people is protected.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Real History in Our Schools. Support federal funding incentives for states and school districts that teach comprehensive history. Oppose federal or state efforts to ban books, censor curricula, or punish teachers for teaching accurate history, while supporting age-appropriate standards developed by educators and historians rather than political appointees. Hate Crime Enforcement. Support robust funding and enforcement for laws addressing hate crimes targeting. Ensure law enforcement agencies have training to recognize and respond to antisemitic, anti-Palestinian, Islamaphobic, anti-Black, anti-Immigrant and all threats and violence.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Safe Campuses and Communities.  Ensure all students and community members can engage in public life, including on college campuses, free from harassment, intimidation, or violence — while protecting the rights of all students to engage in political speech and protest, including on Israel-Palestine. Angie believes in honoring our commitment to our veterans. As a nation, we have a moral obligation to provide the best quality care to those who put their lives on the line. Every war is sold to the American people with speeches about strength and freedom, and every war is paid for, long after the cameras leave, by the people who fought it.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: It is paid for by the soldier who comes home without his legs or his sight, by the Marine who survived the battlefield only to be haunted by it every night, and by the veteran who served with honor but can’t get a good job or find a moment of peace. It is paid for by the spouses and children who bury their loved one who made the ultimate sacrifice and by the families who lose them to suicide years after the battles end. The politicians who rush us into war never send their own sons and daughters, and they rarely stick around to pay the bill.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Angie believes the surest way to protect our troops is to stop sending them into forever wars, and that every veteran who has already served deserves a fully funded, expanded VA, and the benefits they were promised, delivered on time and without excuses. As US Senator, Angie will do everything that she can to make sure that every veteran gets the benefits that they are entitled to receive on time and without delay. She will fight any efforts to dismantle or corporatize the VA and focus on the expansion and improvements of VA services for Florida’s 1.5 million veterans – the second largest veteran population in the country.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Fully fund the VA and hire the doctors, nurses and medical professionals necessary to provide the care that veterans need when they need it. Angie will fight to restore VA job cuts, starting with doctors, nurses, and mental healthcare providers. Repair, modernize and rebuild the infrastructure at VA clinics and hospitals in order to provide the cutting-edge healthcare services our veterans have earned and deserve, including expanding VA facilities and building a full VA medical center in Jacksonville. End the for-profit privatization of VA services so that we do not create a for-profit industry that may cut corners in their service to our honored veterans.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Auto-enroll every new veteran in VA health care and add dental and vision to VA care. Reverse the Medicaid and SNAP cuts hitting veteran families, and restore the ACA tax credits that 440,000 Floridians lost this year. Pass the Major Richard Star Act , allowing more than 50,000 veterans who were injured in combat keep both their full military retirement pay and their VA disability pay, instead of having one reduced because they get the other. Enforce the PACT Act, and ensure the VA pays for care caused by exposure to toxic chemicals. Extend coverage to PFAS, K2, Fort McClellan, and Blue Water Navy veterans.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Expand women’s health care at the VA. I will fund dedicated women’s clinics, enforce the Sampson Act, and require every VA medical center to offer maternity coordination, menopause care, and fertility treatment. Fully fund HUD-VASH, SSVF, and Grant and Per Diem , the programs that cut veteran homelessness 56% since 2010. Build veteran housing on unused VA land , help first-time VA borrowers with down payments, keep struggling borrowers in their homes, and raise adaptive housing grants. Help first-time VA home loan borrowers with a down payment. The VA home loan needs no down payment but still requires closing costs and cash that many young veterans do not have.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Keep veterans in their homes when they fall behind. I will hold the VA and mortgage companies accountable for getting it fully up and running by the November 2026 deadline, make sure every struggling veteran knows it exists, and fight to make it permanent instead of letting it expire in 2030. Prevent veteran suicide through the Saving Our Veterans Lives Act, the BRAVE Act, research on psychedelic-assisted therapy, and VA access to medical cannabis. Expand Veterans Treatment Courts to every county , to ensure our veterans get treatment, not just jail sentences, when they are charged with a crime caused by PTSD, brain injuries, addiction, or mental health problems from their service.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Pass the Military Spouse Hiring Act , which gives employers a tax credit for hiring military spouses. Provide VA child care at every medical center. Open union apprenticeships by trade unions for jobs like electricians, plumbers, and construction workers to make it easier for veterans to get into them, for example by giving credit for skills learned in the military. Restore GI Bill benefits lost to school fraud . Ensure veterans get their benefits restored when lost to schools that misled students and that closed suddenly, or lost approval.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Ensure veterans receive their student housing allowance through breaks so that student veterans have the resources they need to pay rent during breaks between semesters. Put a VA counselor on every major campus, to help student veterans with benefits, disability claims, health care, and career planning. Long-term care where veterans want it. Ensure veterans have access to home health care and add beds in Florida’s state veterans’ homes. Ensure the VA and Medicaid/Medicare work together. Angie will support the Coordinating Care for Senior Veterans and Wounded Warriors Act, which would assign a case manager to veterans enrolled in both.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Pay family caregivers and stop cutting them off. Angie will enforce the protections Congress passed to stop unfair removals and make sure every veteran who needs daily help can get it. Make TRICARE Reserve Select premium-free so that the roughly 130,000 Guard members and reservists without health insurance are covered. Fund full federal benefits for every federal mission so that whenever Guard members are called up for a federal purpose, they receive the full pay, healthcare, retirement credit, and education benefits that come with federal service.

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Ban forced arbitration of reservists’ job rights . Federal law protects their civilian jobs when they’re called to duty. Angie will support reservists in taking their employers to court if their job rights are violated. Enforce the War Powers Act : The Constitution gives Congress the power to declare war, and that means every member should have to go on the record and vote before our troops are sent into combat. Angie Nixon did not rise through political machines or party gatekeepers. She built power in her community. From founding the Melanin Market to support local creators, to opening Natalie’s Nook to fight food insecurity, her work reflects a simple principle:

chunks.title: Priorities - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: This campaign is not asking for permission. Not from corporate donors. Not from party leadership. Not from anyone invested in the status quo.

chunks.title: Meet Angie - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Meet Angie - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate Angie Nixon is a Democratic State Representative, union organizer, mother, and proven fighter born and raised in Jacksonville. In the State House, Angie has been a leading champion for working and middle class Floridians—from expanding childcare for thousands of families; to stopping a major grocery chain from gouging their prices; to leading the resistance to DeSantis’s unfair voting maps.

chunks.title: Meet Angie - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Angie’s pathbreaking leadership includes serving as Executive Director of Florida for All, a statewide coalition that has registered tens of thousands of new voters while raising resources for campaigns and issue-based organizing across the state. At home in Jacksonville, she runs a bookstore and community hub focused on bringing healthy food and educational opportunities to local families.

chunks.title: Meet Angie - Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Angie’s leadership is rooted in her upbringing. She saw her mother work two jobs to make sure she and her brother never went hungry. Throughout elementary school, she was bused across town because her predominantly Black neighborhood school didn’t have adequate resources. Gillespie Candidate Survey Responses to League of Women Voters Palm Beach County Neil J. Gillespie Candidate Survey Responses to League of Women Voters Palm Beach County 1. What reforms to the US immigration system do you support? Why?

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Immigrants are essential for the U.S. economy. We need qualified, vetted, immigrants legally present in America. The de facto open border policy of the Biden administration was wrong. The Biden immigration policy has benefited the legal profession , not the American People. Business is great for immigration lawyers. But some like former lawyer Alexandra Lozano, " La Luz del Camino Legal ", defrauded her clients. Most of my family came to America from Ireland. My maternal great-grandmother was Jewish . I have worked with and support immigrants are naturalized citizens. In Pennsylvania I was a licensed motor vehicle dealer with many immigrant customers .

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: I support secure boarders because we need to know who is in our county, who is in our home. Immigrants' background must be vetted. I support the lawful removal of people who enter the United States illegally, but not the spectacle created by activists confronting ICE. I also support a path to citizenship for immigrants who follow the rules . Photo: Neil Gillespie October 20, 2022 working at NPSG Caddell at Walmart Brooksville FL . This photo was provided to Ballotpedia but not published because it is over two years old. 2. Name your top two legislative priorities for the next Congressional term.

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: My top three legislative priorities (not two) for the next congress: 1. Restore checks and balances in government, separation of powers . Lawyers admitted to practice are officers of the court , part of the judicial branch of government , and must not serve in elected office in the legislature or executive branch . 2. Health care reform . I was born needing craniofacial surgery but my insurance denied coverage for surgery when I was age 18 under a preexisting condition clause. I propose national health coverage, with the ability to opt-out. Trial Lawers add excessive costs , and force doctors to practice defensive medicine. 3. Guarantee the safety of Jews in the United States .

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: America is the promised land that defeated fascism in Europe in 1945 . Unfortunately, Israel cannot protect Jews. Its wars are creating antisemitism worldwide. Prime Minister YitzhakRabin made peace with the Palestinians ( Oslo Accords ). But on Nov-04-1995, an Israeli, Yigal Amir, murdered Rabin , ending the peace plan. The video below was not part of my response. 3. "Freedom of speech" is included in the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. Exactly what does "Freedom of Speech" mean to you?

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Freedom of speech is the right to express opinions and ideas without fear. First Amendment : "Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion , or prohibiting the free exercise thereof ; or abridging the freedom of speech , or of the press ; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances ." That means we are not a "Christian Nation" as some claim. Catholics, Jews, Hindus, and Muslims are not "Christians". Also, the right to "petition the Government for a redress of grievances " is under threat with our current broken court system.

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Twenty-one years ago (in 2005) I sued a Florida law firm for stealing money from my settlement in a civil case. The courts could not resolve the case after 20 years, so I dropped it in 2025. Too many people end up suing their crooked lawyers. One well-known case is " Take Care of Maya ", Maya Kowalski's family, who sued their former attorneys over alleged mishandling of settlement funds. 4. What role do you believe the federal government should play in education at the pre-school level, K-12 level and higher education?

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Parents have the most important role in the education of their children. My parents sent me to Catholic elementary school (grades 1-8) and Catholic high school (grades 9-12) where I was raised in Levittown, PA. The state, when acting " in loco parentis ", is responsible for the child's safely at school. In higher education, students age 18 and older are generally considered adults for legal and institutional purposes. On September 27, 2016, I wrote President Obama about an African-American schoolgirl in Ocala who needed assistance attending public school , which is a federally protected activity under 18 U.S.C. § 245(b)(2)(A) .

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: The Ocala Star-Banner reported a racial incident at West Port High School where 3 students taunted the Black student while waiving Confederate flags. The 15 year-old African-American victim being intimidated by whites was wrongly cited by the police in lieu of arrest. Obama never responded. Florida AG Pam Bondi failed to classify this as a hate crime. ( FS 775.085 ) Note: The League of Women Voters Palm Beach County only published 4 of the 7 responses to questions presented to the candidates. Here are my 3 responses that were not published : 5. Do you believe climate change is a financial threat to the economy of the nation? Why or why not?

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Climate change itself is not a financial threat to the economy, but is an issue to be managed. Extreme reaction to climate change is a financial threat. Obama's 2009 "Cash for Clunkers" program is an example of an extreme reaction. The program scrapped 677,081 vehicles, which was a terrible waste. The Ford Explorer 4WD was the program's top trade-in according to the U.S. DoT. (Wikipedia). Americans still want this type of vehicle. This program "still frustrates car enthusiasts, mechanics, collectors, and budget-minded drivers more than 15 years later. [677,081] vehicles were deliberately destroyed under the Cash for Clunkers program.

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Not recycled after they wore out, not sold to families who needed affordable transportation, and not donated to people struggling to get by. They were intentionally taken out of service and reduced to scrap ." (Yahoo Auto). Instead of scrapping vehicles, Obama could have provided checks to people to buy new vehicles and help the struggling auto industry. 6. Who has the right, Congress or the President, to oversee federal agencies? U.S. District Judge Pamela Chen said, in Court Shorts, Separation of Powers : "This concept of separation of powers is what makes America great. It is absolutely the genius of our democracy."

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: The duty to oversee federal agencies is found in the Constitution. Currently our government is corrupted by a failure of checks and balances , a failure of separation of powers in government . Lawyers admitted to practice are officers of the court , part of the judicial branch of government , and must not serve in elected office in the legislature or the executive branch . Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, lawyers admitted to practice, and who wrongly served as president and vice president, created the current immigration problem with open borders .

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis , a lawyer admitted to practice, is wrongly serving in the executive (as governor), and was able to wrongly take $10 million in taxpayer money, his "cherry on top", for his wife's charity . [ update ] 7. If documentary proof of US citizenship becomes necessary in order to register to vote, how would you help those citizens, especially women, who no longer have or don’t have easy and affordable access to documents to prove citizenship, such as certified birth and marriage certificates?

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate
chunks.text: US citizenship comes with responsibilities. Take action now to get the documents needed to prove citizenship. The best way to prove US citizenship may be your US Passport. Keep your US Passport current. The State Department issues passports and can assist citizens. Perhaps the State Department should serve as a repository for the documents needed to prove citizenship, such as certified birth and marriage certificates. Proof of citizenship is important for secure elections, and a secure border. We The People need to know who is in our country, our home, and who is voting in our elections. chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate

chunks.title: Neil J. Gillespie for U.S. Senate

In this scenario, a Universal Primary Contest occurs. When all candidates for an office have the same party affiliation and the winner will have no opposition in the general election, all voters, regardless of party affiliation, will have the opportunity to vote in this race…"

Judge Moss : When there is a decision from the Supreme Court that's not popular, sometimes that lack of popularity is exactly the way the system is supposed to be working. The example I'll give you there is flag desecration.

chunks.title: Neil 2028
chunks.text: Judge Walton : There was legislation that precluded the burning of a flag. Obviously, the Executive Branch sought to enforce that legislation, and then it ultimately became the responsibility of the courts to make an assessment as to whether that legislation was constitutional. Judge Boasberg : No one's in favor of burning a flag, but the idea is that the Supreme Court believes that the Constitution protects everyone's liberties even for speech you don't like. Judge Moss : And that's what the First Amendment is about. And it's through the separation of powers that we're able to protect that.

chunks.text: Judge Cooper : The courts are the ultimate guardians of the law. We don't have the power of the purse. We don't have an army. Our only power is our ability to defend the Constitution. chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians - Senator Moody
chunks.text: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians - Senator Moody VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians - Senator Moody
chunks.text: WASHINGTON D.C. — Senator Ashley Moody is working to unlock more competition in the drug market by cutting regulatory red tape. Right now, unnecessary regulation in the biosimilar drug approval process at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has led to delays and higher costs for Floridians. Senator Moody’s new legislation would consolidate duplicative regulatory efforts, allow personnel to prioritize getting more biosimilars, which are affordable alternatives to brand name biological drugs, approved, and ultimately lower costs for Floridians.

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians - Senator Moody
chunks.text: The broader usage of affordable alternatives to expensive brand name biological drugs has been shown to collectively save Americans billions of dollars on their health care. “One of my top priorities in the Senate is getting control of runaway costs for Florida families, and that includes the cost of prescription drugs. My new legislation will help families save billions by cutting out unnecessary regulation from the approval process, ultimately reining in drug prices. This is an easy bipartisan fix, and that is why I fought hard to sponsor and pass this bill language out of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pension Committee this week,” said Senator Ashley Moody .

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians - Senator Moody
chunks.text: “In Maryland, we are proud to have the FDA operating in our own backyard. This bill allows the FDA to streamline its review process, increasing efficiency and incentivizing innovation for our life sciences manufacturers in Maryland by getting drugs to market for patients faster. It will reduce confusion, slash the red tape that delays drug approvals, and ultimately, lower prices for patients. I look forward to working with Senator Moody to get this simple fix requested by the career experts at FDA across the finish line,” said Senator Angela Alsobrooks.

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians - Senator Moody
chunks.text: “The Biosimilars Forum commends Senator Moody [and Senator Alsobrooks] for introducing an important bill to streamline and modernize development for safe, effective, and lower-cost biosimilars,” said Juliana M. Reed, executive director of the Biosimilars Forum . “The Forum and its members take immense pride in developing and manufacturing lower-cost biosimilars, and supportive policies are essential to ensure these medicines can reach the patients who need them. Senator Moody’s leadership will help bring more biosimilars to the market more quickly, ensure those biosimilars can reach patients, and improve affordability by lowering everyday health care costs for Americans.”

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians - Senator Moody
chunks.text: · Under the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act of 2009, FDA must require that all biosimilar applications be reviewed by the same review division that handled the reference product. This statute is preventing FDA from promoting the Office of Therapeutic Biologics and Biosimilars to handle biosimilars exclusively and save resources in the other review divisions. · This bill simply strikes Section 351(k)(5)(B) of the Public Health Service Act. · This effort is in line with President Trump’s Great Healthcare Plan to increase health care affordability, making it easier for biosimilar drugs to come to market by reducing regulatory burden.
