chunks.title: About | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Senator Ileana Garcia is a proven leader whose impactful leadership has resulted in landmark legislation and significant funding aimed at enhancing protections, access to services, economic security, and self-sufficiency for Floridians. She is particularly focused on vulnerable populations, such as foster care children and youth, ensuring they have rights, a voice, and the self-confidence to rise.

chunks.title: About | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Her work on homelessness centers on making sure that foster youth are not living on the streets and have access to IDs, driver’s licenses, and comprehensive services that provide opportunities for upward mobility, allowing them to avoid spending their adult lives recovering from traumatic experiences in their youth.

chunks.title: About | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: As a strong advocate for seniors, Senator Garcia fights for legislation and services that provide housing and meet basic needs with dignity and equity. She has worked tirelessly to house homeless seniors and ensure they remain in their homes. Her most significant public fight was against the abuses of Homeowners’ Associations (HOAs) in Miami-Dade, where she provided hands-on services for access to legal help and addressed the ineptitude at the Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR).

chunks.title: About | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Her commitment to environmental issues is evident through her sponsorship, funding, and passage of vital legislation, such as initiatives for Biscayne Bay and Coastal Resiliency. She has also taken a leading role in addressing the challenges posed by single-use plastics, advocating for improved usage and disposal practices. Relentless in her efforts, Senator Garcia is unafraid to challenge the establishment on issues of civil, environmental, and consumer rights. She raises her voice to work on protections and solutions, demonstrating compassion and proactivity in defending the community where she was born and raised.

chunks.title: About | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Before being elected to the Florida Senate in 2020, Senator Garcia dedicated over three decades to the community through her work in radio, television, and advocacy. As a passionate human rights advocate and first-generation Cuban American, her mother and grandmother arrived in 1957 in the very district she now represents, seeking freedom—the essence of the American Dream. Senator Garcia remains actively engaged in advocating for the liberation of political prisoners in Cuba and supporting dissidents in exile, promoting freedom from authoritarian regimes.

chunks.title: About | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: In the Senate, she serves as the Chair of the Appropriations Committee for Criminal and Civil Justice and has previously held the positions of Chair and currently Vice Chair for Children and Families, a cause close to her heart. Senator Garcia has consistently worked to protect families, children, seniors, and even animals. She is sensitive to the needs of her community and remains accessible to her constituents. With a deep commitment to her role, she is seeking to continue serving the constituents of Senate District 36, Miami-Dade.

chunks.title: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands October 25, 2021 | by Jesse Scheckner on Florida Politics The man-made islands are rife with man-made trash. They’re also eroding due to illegal activity. It’s no secret Biscayne Bay is in trouble, and Sen. Ileana Garcia is now working with Miami-Dade County Chief Bay officer Irela Bagué to address one issue that has grown worse since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic: the deterioration of state-owned spoil islands in the bay.

chunks.title: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: The remnants of past bay dredging, spoil islands are small, manmade land masses in the bay. Many today function as miniature beaches and parks complete with sand, mangroves and sea grape, among other native flora, attracting boaters, jet skiers and other aquatic pleasure seekers, as well as an overflow of garbage and debris . The short-term solution to the island trash problem devised months ago by Bagué and the city of Miami, one of the municipalities in Miami-Dade to which the spoil islands have been deeded, was to double the number of weekly trash pickups.

chunks.title: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: But that’s still not enough, and it does nothing to prevent island erosion and physical damage illegally grounded and tethered vessels are causing. Far more work needs to be done — and funded — said Eduardo Tamborrel , Garcia’s legislative aide, who confirmed the Republican Senator has been trying to secure additional funding to maintain and improve the islands. “The municipalities that are managing the islands, there needs to be more financing,” he told Florida Politics. “One of the things the Senator is doing is seeing how she can facilitate helping with the financing of the organizational aspects.”

chunks.title: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: In mid-August, Garcia participated in a workshop Bagué hosted to review the spoil island contracts deeded to Miami and other cities. Much of the workshop focused on curbing illegal charter vessels and livery operations. “Vessels that are illegally grounded or tied to trees are contributing to erosion and physical damage on the spoil islands in Biscayne Bay,” Garcia said in a written statement. “We must do all we can to protect and preserve these tranquil islands that provide our residents and visitors the opportunity to enjoy Florida’s unique natural resources away from the hustle and bustle of Miami’s dynamic urban environment.”

chunks.title: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: To that end, Bagué said, locals and visitors must do their part to maintain the islands and cease “illegal activity, excessive use, irresponsible behavior, and a blatant disregard for nature and our unique wildlife.” “We must all take responsibility and treat Biscayne Bay and these spoil islands the same as we would our backyard, “she said in a statement, adding that the county is working with Garcia, law enforcement and local governments to increase enforcement and prohibit certain uses on the islands. “For decades, Miami-Dade County has spent millions of taxpayer dollars to restore these natural areas and pays weekly for removing trash and debris left behind.”

chunks.title: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Biscayne Bay faces myriad other problems, including seagrass die-off , a record number of manatee deaths this year and repeated, devastating fish kills in the bay caused by wildly fluctuating temperatures and algal blooms . There’s also the increased toxification of the bay due to numerous sewage spills , leaking septic tanks — a multibillion-dollar problem for Miami-Dade County — and stormwater runoff flooding the bay with fertilizer, plastics and other pollutants. A lack of fresh water is also causing the waterway to suffer from “hyper salinity,” Bagué wrote in a nearly three-year-old Miami Herald op-ed .

chunks.title: Ileana Garcia working to secure additional funds to improve Biscayne Bay spoil islands | Ileana Garcia

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia The Socialist Revolution once dismissed as the radical rantings of Bernie Sanders and the Squad have now become the marching orders for Democrats across the country. Led by Joe Biden and his handlers and underscored by violence in our streets, the march toward socialism may not come with a Ridgeway cap or an armed military, but it will most certainly result in the same devastating economic oppression experienced by millions around the world forced to exchange freedom for tyranny.

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: This revolution isn’t just promising a government takeover of health care and a free education. Their master plan is to nationalize our entire economy. Democrats argue that Medicare for All, education for all, housing for all and jobs for all will lead to economic and environmental justice for all. They want us to believe that the meat and medicine shortages in Venezuela can’t happen here. They praise Cuba’s literacy program while ignoring the fact that their technology is frozen in a pre-socialism state; and hope that we’re convinced that Americans standing, desperate and struggling to get by, in breadlines across the country are an impossibility in the 21st Century.

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: But a top-down driven economy by which government creates and rations everything from healthcare to education, and the distribution of jobs and housing is the definition of Market Socialism and the core of what extremists and the Democrats have planned for the American people. The government-dictated rationing of healthcare, housing and jobs will not lead to quality healthcare, nor will it lead to safe housing or better jobs. Let’s examine for a moment how well government-rationed programs that dictate options for people in this country have fared historically.

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Look no further than the failure of our federal government to provide adequate healthcare to the more than nine million Veterans forced into the VA’s labyrinth of hospitals and clinics. Veterans continue to struggle with low access, poor service, antiquated operational systems and bureaucratic processes. Despite the best efforts of some well-intentioned U.S. Representatives, the system remains a cautionary example of what government rationing of healthcare would look like for all Americans if Democrats are successful in November.

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: As Howard Husock pointed out in The Atlantic last year, “Advocates have not been discouraged by the fact that violence and neglect led to the demolition of previous generations of public housing. Nor by the rats, leaks, mold, and lead paint that have now brought the New York City Housing Authority, by far the nation’s largest operator of public housing, under the oversight of a federal monitor.’ Who will monitor the federal government if Democrats are successful in their bid to spend 2.5 trillion dollars to build nearly ten million new government-rationed public housing units?

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: Sanders’ Jobs for All program is built on the misguided promises of government-rationed healthcare, free childcare for all and the Green New Deal, a program that allows the government to ration everything from how much we drive to the kinds of foods we eat. Think about that for minute. What kind of jobs are available at $15 an hour in the construction, healthcare and childcare industries? This flawed, market socialism-driven fantasy is guaranteeing you a job digging ditches, scrubbing hospital floors and changing diapers.

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: That’s not a criticism of the honest day’s work afforded by these jobs, but rather a reality check for the 19-year-old on the quad who’s romanticizing the benefits of socialism while disregarding its decimation of choice and free agency. I appreciate our young people’s wide-eyed optimism for a world where no one wants for anything, but shutter at the notion so many are willing to trade the endless opportunities in front of them for the fairytale being sold to them by snake oil salesmen masquerading as saviors.

chunks.title: Rationing the American Dream | Ileana Garcia
chunks.text: The Democrat party is trying to ration the American Dream and constrain how much our children should dare to achieve. They are asking us to put our faith and our livelihoods in the hands of government instead of each other, to trade hard work for government-rationed handouts and achievement for obedience. They are trying to convince us that America, the greatest experiment in the history of the world, has failed. Someone needs to remind today’s Democrats that prescribed uniformity is not equality, capping potential is not freedom, and demonizing achievement is not justice.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate Accessibility for everyone. Powered by MDW Communications For nearly three decades, one party has controlled Florida’s Legislature—and today holds a supermajority in both chambers. With that much power comes responsibility for the choices Tallahassee makes. This isn’t about party. It’s about accountability. When power goes unchecked, government can stop listening to the people it serves. I’m running because District 36 deserves a representative focused on the pressures families face every day: rising housing and insurance costs, the cost of living, and the growing threat of sea-level rise.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: I will measure every vote by one simple question: Who does this actually serve? My priorities are organized around three questions every Floridian should be able to ask of their government. When something in Florida breaks — the insurance market, the housing market, the budget — the question that matters is who is handed the bill — and too often, the answer is you. Property Insurance That Works for Policyholders +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Florida’s property-insurance market was genuinely broken, and recent reforms did stabilize it — rates slowed, new carriers entered, and far fewer families are stuck with the state insurer of last resort. I will not pretend otherwise. But stability is not the same as affordability. Families here pay among the highest premiums in the country to insure their homes, with more than half of a typical premium going to hurricane coverage alone. And policyholders have spent years paying a surcharge on every bill for the unpaid claims left behind by the companies that collapsed — even as Tallahassee takes credit for rate cuts.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Reform the state insurance framework so that families hit by predictable losses can actually recover, rather than being left with denied claims and added fees. Demand transparency and fairness in how the cost of a company’s collapse ends up on your bill. Treat insurance as the cost-of-living emergency it is for this district, where the insurance bill is as urgent as the rent or the mortgage. Tax Fairness for Renters and Working Families +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Florida already has one of the most regressive tax systems in the nation: it takes a far larger share of a working family’s income than of a wealthy household’s. As proposals move to cut homestead property taxes, we must raise the objection no one is raising on behalf of the majority of this district who rent: if the exemption only reaches homeowners but the lost revenue is replaced by a higher sales tax, you do not get relief — you get the bill twice: in your rent and in everything you buy. Insist that any tax change be measured by its effect on renters and working families, not only on homestead owners.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Oppose shifting the cost of tax cuts onto regressive sales taxes that fall hardest on those who can least afford them. Protect funding for the local services — first responders, parks, road maintenance — that a sudden revenue hole would put at risk. The Power Bill the State Has Its Hand On +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: I will not insult you by pretending a state senator can lower the price of groceries or gas — those are set by national and global forces no one in Tallahassee controls, and any candidate who claims otherwise is not being straight with you. Your electric bill is different. Part of it is fuel and storm recovery, which the state does not set and the company cannot mark up. But part of it is a base rate and a guaranteed company profit that a state commission approves — and that guaranteed profit is among the highest granted to any utility in the country. The state’s own consumer advocate has put the cost of it in the hundreds of millions of dollars, drawn from customers’ bills.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: The commission that approved it is not even required by law to consider whether families can afford the result. Fight for legislation that requires the utility commission to weigh affordability for families — something current law does not require it to do. Be honest about the limits: a senator cannot set a rate or order a bill lowered, but a senator votes on who sits on that commission and on the laws that bind it. Hold the state accountable only for what it controls — the base rate, the guaranteed profit, and the rules — while telling the truth about the fuel and storm costs it does not.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Make sure a coming driver of your bill — the enormous power and water demands of new data centers — is paid by the companies that profit from them: no public subsidies, no tax exemptions, and no stranded costs left on the ratepayer when a site shuts down. Standing With Families as Sea Levels Rise +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: A state senator cannot raise a single street above the water — that is the work of our cities, and they are doing it. But the State of Florida writes the insurance rules that decide whether a family whose home floods can recover, and the state funds the grant programs — what Tallahassee calls “resilience” — that pay for the pumps, drainage, and seawalls that help communities adapt. Those are decisions a state senator votes on. Fight every year to fund the state’s flood-protection grants and to bring those dollars home to District 36’s communities. Reform flood and property-insurance rules so families whose homes flood are not left to absorb the loss alone.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Make sure the state shows up as a partner to the communities already doing the hard work of adaptation. Repeal the law that deleted “climate change” from most of Florida’s statutes. A state cannot plan for a risk it will not name — and the market prices that denial into your premium.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: After the Surfside collapse took ninety-eight lives, the state did the right thing: it required older buildings to be inspected and to fund the repairs they had long deferred. No one should undo that. But the state ordered the repairs and built no way to help families pay for them — and now, as those costs come due, the only help for an owner facing a five- or six-figure assessment is a county loan they have to repay. Tallahassee mandated the cost and handed people a loan application. Build the state assessment-relief fund that does not exist, so families are not forced to sell homes they have lived in for decades to comply with a safety law.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Keep faith with the safety mandate while insisting the state share the cost of a decision it made. Be honest about what these assessments are: bills that were always coming, which the law brought into the open — and which families should not have to shoulder alone.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Here is something Tallahassee does not advertise. There are federal dollars — our own tax dollars — available to cover working people in this community who fall in the gap: earning too much to qualify for help and too little to afford a plan. The state turned that money down. So those dollars go to other states — and the cost of caring for the uninsured comes back to us anyway, in the county sales tax and property tax that keep our safety-net hospital open. We pay our federal taxes and watch the help go elsewhere; then we pay again, locally, to cover the gap here at home. This is arithmetic, not ideology: we pay twice — once to Washington, once to the county — and get nothing back for it.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Fight to bring our own federal dollars home to cover working families in the coverage gap, rather than sending those dollars to other states. Be straight about the limits: when Washington let health-insurance subsidies lapse, premiums jumped here higher than almost anywhere — and a state senator cannot put a federal subsidy back. I will say so plainly, and fight for the state-level steps that could cushion it. Treat the cost of the uninsured as what it is — a charge already sitting on your county taxes, whether or not anyone admits it.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Some issues call for statewide standards. But Tallahassee shouldn’t dictate every decision to every community. Our cities and neighborhoods know their needs best. I’ll fight to keep local decisions local—and make sure the people closest to the problem have a real voice in solving it, and that is you.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: By the counts kept by Florida’s cities and counties, the Legislature has filed dozens of bills each session restricting the authority of local governments — on wages, on scheduling, on rent, on housing, even on protecting outdoor workers from the heat — and more. Most fail; but the Legislature files them again and again, session after session, year after year, and the ones that pass do real damage, including penalties aimed at the local officials who dare to cross Tallahassee. This is not a complaint about any single law. It is a pattern: a steady transfer of self-government to the capital.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Defend the constitutional home-rule authority of cities and counties against the relentless tide of preemption. Trust the officials closest to you — the ones whose offices you can walk into — to address the problems they know best. Be honest that the trend is not absolute: when the state has wisely left decisions in local hands, that judgment deserves to be defended and extended, not reversed.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Florida’s housing crisis is real, and the state’s signature housing law has produced some new homes and modestly narrowed the shortage. But it overrode local communities’ own planning to do so, and it has delivered only a small fraction of the housing the state needs. We can do better than seizing local control in exchange for a fraction of the fix. Support affordable-housing approaches that give communities a real say in what gets built in them. Hold large state housing programs accountable for results measured in homes families can actually afford. Protecting Communities’ Power to Adapt +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: On flood and stormwater resilience, the state has so far left local governments the authority to act — which is why our cities have been able to write their own stronger building standards and protect their neighborhoods. That local authority is one of the few we still hold, and it is worth guarding. Protect local governments’ power to set stronger flood and storm-resistance standards from any future preemption. Defend Florida’s storm-resistant building standards from being weakened or repealed, and back the communities planning seriously for sea-level rise. Keeping Government Out of Private Life +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: The same instinct that says the capital should not overrule your city says it should not reach into your home. Decisions about your family, your faith, and your private life belong to you — not to Tallahassee. Many of the families who built this district know from their own histories exactly what it costs when a government decides it may dictate who people are and how they must live. A government that respects its limits stays out of the places that were never its business. Defend the principle that the state has no place legislating your private life, your family, or your conscience.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Protect the separation of church and state — your right to practice your faith, or not, free of government pressure either way. Keep the focus of state power where it belongs: on the costs and decisions that are actually the state’s job, not on policing private life. Accountability is at the heart of good government. When one party controls every lever of power for too long, accountability disappears. Leaders stop listening, mistakes go unchecked, and voters pay the price.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: I’m running to bring accountability back to Tallahassee—and to make sure your voice is heard. We must break the stronghold Tallahassee has over the municipalities and counties and are not listening to the people they govern. Your voice is in your vote, and I would appreciate your confidence and support. Restoring Accountability to Tallahassee +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Look honestly at what a generation of unchecked power has built. When the insurance market broke, the rescue went to the companies, and a surcharge went onto your bill. As tax changes advance, working families are being asked to pay for tax cuts they may never receive. And each time a community closest to you tries to act on your behalf, it is overruled or punished for crossing Tallahassee. None of this is an accident. It is what power that answers to no one does — it protects itself, and it sends the invoice to everyone else.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Consider the commission that sets the rules behind your power bill. The last time it denied the largest utility a rate increase was in 2010; the commissioners who cast that vote were denied reconfirmation and off the commission within months; and no commission has denied that company an increase in the years since. The people who said no were replaced, and the decisions have run one direction ever since. You can draw your own conclusion about who such a body answers to. Provide the check and balance that one-party supermajority control has erased — a vote and a voice that answer to this district, not to the capital.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Insist on transparency and real oversight of what state decisions cost working families. Measure every bill by a single test: does this serve the people of District 36, or the powerful interests closest to power? Following the Public’s Money in Our Schools +

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Florida now spends billions of public dollars on what the state calls private-school scholarships — vouchers, in plain terms — and on charter schools, and there is good in that record — families have used scholarships and their children have gone on to college, and competition has pushed some public schools to improve. I will not take that away. But the state has arranged the system so that the most basic accountability questions cannot be answered. Students who take scholarship money to attend private schools are not required to take the same statewide test that public schools are graded on, so no one can say whether the public is getting its money’s worth.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Charter schools are public, and their students take the same test — but when one closes, as hundreds have already, the state does not track why, or what happened to the students. And when public dollars are paid out as rent and fees to private operators, that money does not come back to the public school system if the charter school fails. Public money should be traceable. Right now, by the state’s own design, it is not. Require that public dollars spent on scholarships and charter schools be measured by results the public can actually see. Demand that the state track school closures, and account for the students and the public funds when a school fails.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Insist on transparency wherever public money flows to private operators, including the leases and management fees that ordinary families never get to see. This district was built in large part by families who know, from their own histories, exactly what it means when power runs only to the center and stops answering to the people. That instinct — that government should be close, accountable, and answerable — is not partisan. It is the oldest American idea there is. It is the idea I will carry to Tallahassee.

chunks.title: Why I Am Running — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: District 36 deserves someone in Tallahassee who answers to you, and only to you. That is what I am offering: I will show up, I will tell you the truth about what this office can and cannot do, and I will measure every vote by who it actually serves.

chunks.title: Meet George Lavín — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: I was born in Miami, and though my childhood took me overseas, every year I’ve spent in Florida I’ve spent right here in this community. My early childhood ran through Brussels and then Barcelona — where we landed in late 1975, just after the end of the dictatorship and the start of Spain’s return to democracy. The family then settled in Coral Gables in the early 1980s. I spent my school years here: St. Hugh Catholic School, Christopher Columbus High School (¡Adelante!), and my degree from FIU, after which I left for graduate school.

chunks.title: Meet George Lavín — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: After more than a decade away in New York — where I lived through the horror of 9/11 and saw firsthand the innate goodness of ordinary people in a time of terror — I returned to Florida twenty years ago, to Coral Gables and then to West Miami. As a legal consultant who works with former prosecutors, law firms, and corporate legal departments, I bring a sharp analytical mind and a deep sense of civic responsibility to everything I do.

chunks.title: Meet George Lavín — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: I come from people who kept having to leave — some pushed out by politics, some by need. My family’s roots run from Spain to Cuba and Canada. My father was born in Havana — a first-generation Cuban, but as Cuban as one could be. My mother was born in Montreal — where her family had gone after my grandfather, at just nineteen years old, fled Cuba to stay out of a Machado jail — and she was raised in Havana after they returned to Cuba. When the Revolution came, she was at university studying architecture — sadly, a degree she would never get to finish.

chunks.title: Meet George Lavín — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Her counterrevolutionary activities risked her arrest by the communist regime and made it impossible for her to stay; the Canadian government got her out — the same Canada that had taken my grandfather in a generation before — and she settled in New York, having to start from zero, like so many other exiles. My father was already an economist, a university graduate. He believed the Batista dictatorship had to be ousted, but broke with the change he’d wanted for Cuba when it turned to communism — one dictatorship traded for another. He, too, left for New York and also had to start from zero. Neither of them ever went back to Cuba.

chunks.title: Meet George Lavín — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: Two exiles, two anti-communists who raised four boys, above all, to question everything, show compassion, and live a moral life. It is a family history that taught me early what it costs when a government stops answering to the people it governs.

chunks.title: Meet George Lavín — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: I registered as a Democrat at eighteen — by conviction, not by inheritance, and not in spite of how I was raised but because of it. My parents, like their parents before them, poured everything into our education, and the schools they chose taught us to think for ourselves, serve others, and live a moral life. Over the years I watched my parents come to feel that the party they had long called home no longer reflected the principles they had held their whole lives. They taught me that principle comes before party — and that lesson is at the heart of why I am running.

chunks.title: Meet George Lavín — George Lavín for State Senate
chunks.text: My husband and I — married nine years — have built our life here, guided by the example of both our parents’ marriages, each lasting more than fifty-five years: proof that communication, compassion, and compromise can bridge almost any divide. Now I’m ready to give back — with new ideas, fresh energy, and an unwavering commitment to making every citizen and resident feel seen, heard, and represented. One party has held all the power in Tallahassee for too long, without having to answer to the people it governs. I’m running to make them answer.

chunks.title: Press Releases
chunks.text: In 2008, Betsie Gallardo was sentenced to a five-year sentence at Broward Correctional Institution for biting and kicking a Collier County sheriff’s deputy. Betsie was born HIV-positive and was an immigrant from Haiti. Due to her condition, she was sentenced to live out what was to be the remainder of her life in prison. In 2010, Betsie was diagnosed with late-stage cancer and made a last wish to live her remaining days outside of prison. Her adoptive mother, Jessica Bussert, who adopted Betsie 17 years ago on a mission trip, pleaded with legislators to release Betsie.

chunks.title: Press Releases
chunks.text: Upon hearing the case, Representative Campbell moved to get Betsie released. Shortly after, the Florida Parole Commission voted to approve Gallardo’s medical release from prison to live her remaining days outside. On Monday, January 31, 2011, Betsie Gallardo passed away surrounded by family and friends. Representative Campbell is glad Betsie was able to live out her remaining days with her family and wishes them the best. "I'm just overjoyed to take her home to Indiana to die with dignity.” -Jessie Bussert, Betsie’s mother

chunks.text: Miami, Florida - On Yesterday, October 17, 2014, the Department of Homeland Security announced that they will begin implementation of a Haitian Family Reunification Parole (HFRP) Program to expedite family reunification for Haitian family members of U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents of the U.S. and to promote safe, legal and orderly migration from Haiti to the United States.

chunks.title: Wancito Francius for State Representative District 108
chunks.text: The Nathan Emmanuel Francius Autism Support and Resources Act This Act shall be known and may be cited as the "Nathan Emmanuel Francius Autism Support and Resources Act." (a) The Legislature finds that Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects many Florida children, requiring specialized resources and interventions for their development and success. (b) The Legislature recognizes the critical need for tools, programs, and professional support to address the unique needs of children with ASD. (c) The Legislature intends to allocate funding for schools and professionals to enhance support for children with ASD.

chunks.title: Wancito Francius for State Representative District 108
chunks.text: (a) "Autism Spectrum Evaluation (ASE) Program" means a program providing tools, resources, and interventions for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. (b) "Registered Behavior Technician (RBT)" means a paraprofessional certified in behavioral health, specializing in working with children diagnosed with ASD. (c) "Eligible Schools" means public or private schools in Florida operating for at least two years. (a) The Department of Education (DOE) shall allocate $3,000,000 for Autism Spectrum Evaluation (ASE) Programs. (b) Eligible Schools may receive up to $40,000 each to purchase autism-specific tools, including: Other educational resources for children with ASD.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative A Visionary Leader, Advocate, and Community Champion Fabián Basabe is a devoted family man, entrepreneur, environmental advocate, and passionate supporter of the arts. Born in New York City to an American mother and Ecuadorian father, Basabe was immersed in a myriad of cultures from an early age. He moved to Quito, Ecuador at age six and attended S.E.K. Elementary School, embracing Latin American traditions before relocating to Miami Beach in 1987.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: In Miami Beach, Basabe witnessed firsthand the city’s transformation into a global destination as his family restored the historic Boulevard and Breakwater Hotels on Ocean Drive. His early experiences working in the family businesses gave him a deep appreciation for Miami Beach’s diversity and growth. After graduating from Cheshire Academy in Connecticut, Basabe pursued International Relations at Pepperdine University in Malibu, California, where his interest in television media and writing grew. Following college, he was a correspondent on E! Entertainment’s “Young, Rich and Famous” and “Filthy Rich Cattle Drive”, TLC’s “Simple Life to Social Life”, and even had a guest appearance on Oprah.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: In 2007, Basabe and his wife, Martina Borgomanero, made Miami Beach their permanent home, raising their son Brando and deepening their commitment to the community. Basabe’s philanthropic efforts have supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, Operation Smile, Spirituality for Kids, and the IBLA Foundation. He has also written for LA Confidential, Paper Magazine and Gotham, among others. In 2022, Basabe was elected to the Florida State House of Representatives for District 106—a district long considered one of the state’s most challenging.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Through his unwavering dedication, he has become a champion for the people, building bipartisan coalitions, restoring record funding to his district and earning the respect of many leaders across the aisle. Basabe’s legislative priorities focus on standing firm for educators, law enforcement, and first responders while carrying the struggles of the most vulnerable in his heart. A true friend to the environment, he continues to advocate for environmental preservation and sustainable growth.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Reelected for a second term in 2024 with broad support, Basabe exemplifies integrity, honesty, and character in public service, while his leadership reflects a tireless fight for the values that unite communities and a commitment to improving the quality of life for all Floridians. Fabián Basabe’s journey—from entrepreneur and cultural advocate to respected Legislator—demonstrates his unyielding passion for serving the people of District 106 and beyond.

chunks.title: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative As your elected representative, I am proud to serve as a dedicated family man and a long-standing resident of this incredible district. Together, we have achieved tremendous milestones, navigating two primaries and two general elections to solidify our seat at the state’s table in Tallahassee. Our district is now a cornerstone of Florida’s supermajority, ensuring that our voices are heard and our priorities addressed.

chunks.title: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: When I first ran for office, I was determined to challenge partisanship and bring people together. Today, I remain committed to uniting our community around shared goals to achieve real progress. As a key member of the majority party, I have successfully worked to pass critical legislation and secure funding to meet the needs of District 106. We are revitalizing small businesses, advocating for homeowners and taxpayers, enhancing public safety, modernizing our infrastructure, protecting our beaches and ensuring dignity and care for our elderly. These efforts are only the beginning and I will continue to fight for solutions to improve the quality of life for every resident.

chunks.title: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Our challenges are significant, but so are our opportunities. By working together with common sense and determination, we will continue to revitalize and secure our district for generations to come. I am honored to represent you and invite you will join in as we build on our success and strive for even greater achievements. Let’s keep this momentum going—together. “Florida State Fraternal Order of Police believes in the character and moral fiber of Fabian Basabe. We were so impressed with this young man's fervor in wanting to make his district flourish again that we unanimously voted to endorse his candidacy for State Representative in district 106”.

chunks.title: luciabaezgeller.com
chunks.text: The daughter of a Cuban father and Colombian mother, Lucia grew up witnessing the courage and sacrifice that define the American Dream. Her father fled communism in Cuba in the 1980s, surviving a month with almost no food or water while seeking refuge at the Peruvian Embassy before finally reaching the United States. Lucia was raised by her single mother, who worked multiple jobs to ensure her daughter had every opportunity to succeed. Lucia became the first in her family to attend college — an experience that shaped her lifelong commitment to education and standing up for equal opportunity for every resident of District 106.

chunks.title: luciabaezgeller.com
chunks.text: From 2005 to 2020, Lucia taught English and Language Arts at Miami Beach Senior High, where she connected with and inspired thousands of students. Her leadership in education earned her the National Education Association’s Political Advocate of the Year Award in 2013, and she has worked with numerous organizations dedicated to expanding educational opportunity, including the Educational Excellence School Advisory Council, the Association of Latino Administrators and Superintendents, the Hispanic Scholarship Fund, and the League of Women Voters.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: Home > Government > Board of County Commissioners > District 5 > About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez The Honorable Vicki L. Lopez was appointed to the Miami-Dade Board of County Commissioners and sworn in on November 19, 2025, to represent District 5, bringing decades of public service, community leadership, and professional experience to her role. Commissioner Lopez is a graduate of the University of Notre Dame, where she earned a Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: Commissioner Lopez has an extensive record of service at both the state and local levels. She was elected to the Florida House of Representatives in 2022 and has since been reelected, advocating for policies that strengthen communities and improve quality of life. Earlier in her career, she served on the Lee County Commission from 1990 to 1993, gaining firsthand experience in local government and constituent services.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: Her statewide leadership includes appointments by multiple Florida governors to key boards and task forces. These include serving as Chairman of the Governor’s Ex-Offender Task Force, Vice Chair of the Department of Corrections Reentry Advisory Council, and Chairman and Treasurer of the Prison Rehabilitative Industries and Diversified Enterprises Board. She has also contributed to juvenile justice reform as a member of the Florida Senate Juvenile Justice Education Work Group and played a role in shaping tourism policy through the Florida Tourism Commission’s Industry/Government Affairs Committee.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: A practicing Catholic, Commissioner Lopez is deeply committed to civic engagement, personal well-being, and service to others. Outside of her public service, she enjoys cooking and entertaining, horseback riding, meditation, music, reading, travel, water sports, yoga, walking, and most importantly, spending time with family. With a strong foundation in public service and a deep commitment to her community, Commissioner Lopez serves the residents of Miami-Dade County with experience, integrity, and dedication. 1700 Convention Center Drive, 1st Floor, Contact Us | About the Commissioner Request Public Records

On behalf of Miami Dade County, he also served on key regional bodies such as the Downtown Development Authority, the Miami River Commission, the South Florida Regional Transportation Authority (Tri-Rail), and the Southeast Florida Transportation Council. In 2006, he was selected by his colleagues to serve as Chairman of the Miami-Dade Board of County Commissioners, where he presided over the County’s legislative branch and oversaw the Office of Protocol, Intergovernmental Affairs and the Office of the Commission Auditor.

chunks.title: Home - My WordPress Site
chunks.text: Barreiro has been recognized by numerous local, state, and federal organizations for his leadership and service. In 1999, he founded the Barreiro Foundation, a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting underprivileged youth and the elderly. A lifelong South Floridian, Barreiro is an alumnus of St. Theresa Catholic School, Christopher Columbus High School and attended the University of Miami and Florida International University. He is the President of BABJ Investment Corporation, CEO of Fatima Home Care and Partner at IUSA Water. Born in Clearwater, Florida to Cuban immigrant parents, he lives with his wife, Zoraida, and they are the proud parents of Bianca and Bruno Antonio.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: As a former public school teacher in Miami-Dade, Ashley has experienced firsthand the importance of investing in our schools. Equity starts with providing the space and resources to underserved youth to develop the skills they need in order to compete in our changing economy. Our students need unique resources to meet their specific needs to prepare them for successful and full lives, where test preparation isn’t emphasized more than intellectual development.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Florida needs a fair funding formula to ensure inner-city school districts are receiving equitable funding for resources like books and programing for the creative and performing arts, increased wages for Florida teachers to attract new talent and reduce the student-to-teacher ratio in public schools, and a guarantee that all schools are ADA compliant and provide fair and equal opportunities to students with disabilities.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Miami-Dade’s housing affordability crisis is in dire need for solutions. Our county’s State of Emergency is due to families’ inability to stay in their homes and find safe housing. As housing costs skyrocket while wages remain stagnant, it’s imperative that we provide affordable housing opportunities to the residents of Florida. By increasing the accessibility of housing vouchers, repairing and improving existing public housing, taxing house flipping and other speculative real estate practices, and instating affordable housing requirements for new real estate development projects we can level the playing field for those who are simply trying to live.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Miami-Dade County is ground-zero for climate change. Addressing sea level rise for our coastal communities, and providing clean air and water to Floridians should be a top priority in the State Senate. Legal and financial consequences must be levied against polluters, holding them accountable for the destruction of our beaches, water supply, and air. We have a small window of opportunity to enact changes to protect our environment to make sure it flourishes for generations to come.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: As a former public defender, Ashley Gantt has seen the unequitable effects of a broken criminal justice system and we must work towards establishing more restorative justice programs, increased mental health services, and alternatives to incarceration for our youth. Florida is better when we work together to establish programs to reduce recidivism and support the reintegration of returning citizens to our communities.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Effective and reliable transportation is the cornerstone of a region’s economic health. Investing in eco-friendly public transportation will help create green jobs, improve accessibility for residents in densely populated urban areas, and expand workforce opportunities regionally. Supporting Small Business & Job Creation

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Small businesses are the backbone of our community’s economic sustainability and growth. As State Senator, Ashley will work to ensure equitable pathways to support and opportunities so that small businesses can thrive and grow. Good paying jobs are in dire need to ensure Floridians can afford the rising costs of living, and by attracting employers to our community, we can do just that.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate Ashley Gantt is an attorney, educator, and public servant running to represent Miami-Dade in the State Senate. From the classroom to the courtroom, Ashley has dedicated her career to serving her community. She hopes to bring her experiences to Tallahassee to advocate for the residents of her district.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Ashley V. Gantt, Esq. is the founder partner of Bracy Davis, Gantt, & Rayner, P.A. In 2007 Ashley graduated from the University of Florida with a Bachelor of Arts degree in English and became a Teach for America Mississippi Delta Corps (TFA) member. She dedicated two years to national community service, with a mission to close the achievement gap in the Greater Delta region. Ashley returned home to teach in Miami-Dade County Public Schools for seven years before beginning law school. Gantt was a high school dance-team coach and a Miami Dolphins Cheerleader.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: In 2016, Ashley graduated from NSU Shepard Broad College of Law. While in law school, Ms. Gantt served as chapter Secretary and President of the Black Law Students Association. She is a member of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc. and the University of Florida Association of Black Alumni South Florida chapter. Upon her admission to the Florida Bar, Ashley became a Broward County Assistant Public Defender, serving the citizens of Broward County for over two years. She received recognition for her work, earning two consecutive “Hat Trick” Awards from the Broward Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys for attaining not guilty verdicts in at least three successive trials.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: In 2021, Ashley pivoted from working at a large firm to opening her law firm, Gantt Legacy Law, P.A. She specializes in Criminal Defense, Estate Planning and Probate, and Personal Injury. Various life experiences influenced her areas of specialization and continue to fuel her ambition and drive as a practitioner.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Ms. Gantt continues to be active in her community, serving on the executive board of the T.J. Reddick Bar Association as corresponding secretary, recording secretary, President-Elect and President in the 2020-2021 fiscal year. Ashley is a board member for the Gwen S. Cherry Black Women Lawyers Association and a Florida Bar Wm. Reece Smith Jr. Leadership Academy Fellow. Ms. Gantt also served as the District 2 Trust member on the Citizens’ Independent Transportation Trust in Miami-Dade County. Lastly, Ms. Gantt is an adjunct professor at Nova Southeastern University College of Law.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34 Leader. Advocate. Servant. For District 34. “Understanding our history is essential to building our future.” Elizabeth Jeanty is a resident of Florida Senate District 34, an entrepreneur, community leader, media personality, historian, and candidate for the Florida State Senate. With more than 20 years of experience in nonprofit leadership, business development, and civic engagement, she has dedicated her career to empowering communities through education, advocacy, and service.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: A Miami-Dade County resident for over 27 years, Elizabeth was born in the Dominican Republic to Haitian parents. A background that has given her a lived understanding of the Haitian, Latina, and Black communities that make up much of District 34. Fluent in English, Spanish, Haitian Creole, and French, she has built her life's work around bridging cultures, preserving history, and creating opportunity for the many communities she calls her own, and has become a trusted voice across South Florida's diverse neighborhoods.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth is the Executive Director and Chairwoman of the Haitian American Historical Society (HAHS), where she leads initiatives dedicated to preserving and promoting the contributions of Haitians to American history. Under her leadership, HAHS has educated thousands about the legacy of the Chasseurs-Volontaires de Saint-Domingue — the more than 550 freemen of color who fought alongside American forces during the Revolutionary War — whose sacrifices are commemorated through the annual Haitian Monument events in Savannah, Georgia.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: She is also the host of The Power of Women Show on WLQY 1320 AM in Miami, where she educates and engages the community on issues related to history, civic participation, economic opportunity, leadership, and community empowerment. As the founder of Eliza Consulting Agency LLC and a licensed Florida real estate professional, she has helped individuals, families, and entrepreneurs across every background navigate business, housing, and financial opportunities, always advocating for economic mobility and self-sufficiency.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: As a candidate for the Florida State Senate, District 34, Elizabeth's platform is centered on housing affordability, insurance costs, infrastructure and flood resilience, and responsible local governance. The issues most directly shaping daily life for District 34 families, regardless of background. She believes leadership is not simply holding a title; it is showing up, listening, educating, and delivering meaningful results for every resident she serves.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth's story reflects the full identity of the community she seeks to represent. She carries the shared experience of Haitian, Latina, and Black families across the district. The same challenges of building wealth, owning a home, and securing a future for the next generation. She believes that preserving history and expanding opportunity is not the work of one community alone, but a shared responsibility that unites every family calling this district home. Her leadership is rooted in that shared struggle and shared possibility, building bridges rather than drawing lines, and delivering results for all. Expanding access to affordable homes and protecting homeowners across District 34.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: Fighting for relief and fairness for families struggling with rising insurance premiums. Investing in strong infrastructure and flood protection to keep our communities safe and resilient. Promoting transparency, accountability, and leadership that puts residents first. Service is not about a title. It’s about showing up, listening, educating, and delivering results that change lives.

chunks.title: Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34 Elizabeth Jeanty is running for Florida State Senate to make our communities safer, more affordable, and full of opportunity. Every student deserves the resources to succeed and a bright future. Healthcare is a right, not a privilege. I will fight to make it accessible for all. Building safer, stronger neighborhoods and supporting working families. Creating good-paying jobs, supporting small businesses, and growing our local economy. Leadership That Listens. Service That Delivers.

chunks.title: Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: For too many families, the cost of living keeps rising while the government feels further away. Rent, home insurance, flooding, public safety, healthcare, and the challenges facing small businesses are not partisan issues - they are everyday realities. Elizabeth Jeanty is running to bring practical, accountable leadership to Tallahassee and ensure every community in District 34 has a voice. Leadership is not about power, it’s about service. I’m not running to hold office — I’m running to make a difference. Your support helps us build a stronger future for District 34. Join our team and help make a difference in our community. Sign up for updates and be the first to know what’s happening.

chunks.title: In the Community | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth Jeanty has worked alongside community volunteers, emergency-response professionals and Miami-Dade Fire Rescue personnel to promote public safety and emergency preparedness. She has also attended and spoken at community events addressing important issues affecting families throughout South Florida, standing with residents from Haiti, Cuba, Honduras, Nicaragua and other communities facing uncertainty due to changes in federal immigration policy. Elizabeth believes that strong communities require preparation, cooperation and responsive government.

chunks.title: In the Community | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: She supports secure borders and respect for the law while also advocating for clear communication, due process and an orderly, humane approach for families affected by government decisions. June 11th, 2020 North Miami • June 3, 2020 Miramar • February, 2024 North Miami Advocating for Justice and Accountable Leadership

chunks.title: In the Community | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth has helped organize and participated in peaceful community rallies calling for change, fair intervention and accountability from leaders in cases affecting communities throughout Miami-Dade and Broward counties. These rallies bring residents, advocates and local leaders together, creating a peaceful space for people to be heard and encouraging constructive engagement with elected officials and law enforcement. Her involvement demonstrates her commitment to standing with affected communities, uniting people around difficult issues and working toward fair, practical solutions. May 2017 • May 2020 • June, 2022 • November, 2025 Supporting Families Through Annual Food Distributions

chunks.title: In the Community | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: Every year, Elizabeth Jeanty partners with donors, local organizations and community leaders to provide food and essential assistance to families in need. These annual distributions allow her to serve residents directly while hearing about the challenges they face. Her continued commitment reflects her belief that leadership means building strong partnerships, showing up consistently and working together to support the community. Educating, Empowering and Preserving Our History

chunks.title: In the Community | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: Through the People Action Committee, Elizabeth promotes citizenship, voter education and civic participation. As Executive Director of the Haitian American Historical Society, she also preserves Haitian history and leads the annual Savannah commemoration honoring the Chasseurs-Volontaires de Saint-Domingue and their contributions to the American Revolution. Bringing Community Leadership to International Forums

chunks.title: In the Community | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: As Executive Director of the Haitian American Historical Society, Elizabeth Jeanty served as a speaker at an international forum held at the United Nations. She discussed how artificial intelligence can help address challenges affecting Haiti and support development in healthcare, education, entrepreneurship, workforce training and other essential sectors. She also participated in discussions at the Organization of American States, where she advocated for responsible and accountable government and stronger institutions that serve the people.

chunks.title: In the Community | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: These experiences demonstrate her ability to represent her community, contribute to international policy conversations and bring innovative ideas to the challenges facing communities locally and abroad. “Leadership means showing up consistently, listening to families, and working together to support the community.”

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Senator Alexis Calatayud is a champion for generational upward mobility, focused on expanding educational and economic opportunities for Miami-Dade residents. Her leadership has led to landmark legislation and significant funding aimed at achieving economic security and self-sufficiency for Floridians. Key initiatives include lowering the cost of living, enhancing community affordability, improving access to affordable housing, children's health insurance, and investing in early childhood education. She also serves on the Jackson Memorial Health System Public Health Trust.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: La Senadora Alexis Calatayud es defensora de la movilidad ascendente generacional, enfocada en ampliar oportunidades educativas y económicas para los residentes de Miami-Dade. Su liderazgo ha resultado en legislación histórica y financiación significativa para lograr la seguridad económica y la autosuficiencia de los floridanos. Sus iniciativas clave incluyen reducir el costo de vida, mejorar la asequibilidad comunitaria, ampliar el acceso a vivienda asequible, seguro médico infantil e invertir en educación temprana. También sirve en el Fideicomiso de Salud Pública del Sistema Jackson Memorial.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Before being elected to the Florida Senate in 2022, Senator Calatayud dedicated over a decade to advocacy and policy roles in education reform. Currently, as Community Engagement Liaison for the Miami-Dade and Monroe County Early Learning Coalition, she facilitates national learning exchanges. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she served as Chief Lobbyist and Legislative Affairs Director for the Florida Department of Education, advocating for impactful education policies.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Antes de ser elegida al Senado de Florida en 2022, la Senadora Calatayud dedicó más de una década a roles de defensa y política en reforma educativa. Actualmente, como Enlace de Participación Comunitaria de la Coalición de Aprendizaje Temprano de Miami-Dade y Monroe, facilita intercambios nacionales de aprendizaje. Durante la pandemia de COVID-19, sirvió como Cabildera Principal y Directora de Asuntos Legislativos del Departamento de Educación de Florida.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: A passionate human rights advocate and granddaughter of Cuban political asylum seekers, Senator Calatayud collaborates with nonprofits to support political prisoners and dissidents in exile and promote freedom from authoritarian regimes. She has also trained over 500 university student leaders on higher education affordability issues.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Defensora apasionada de los derechos humanos y nieta de exiliados políticos cubanos, la Senadora Calatayud colabora con organizaciones sin fines de lucro para apoyar a presos políticos y disidentes en el exilio y promover la libertad de los regímenes autoritarios. También ha capacitado a más de 500 líderes estudiantiles universitarios sobre la asequibilidad de la educación superior. In the Senate, she serves as Chair of the Education Postsecondary Committee and Vice Chair of the Education Pre-K–12 Committee , along with various appropriation committees. With a deep commitment to her role, she is running for election in 2026 to continue serving the constituents of Senate District 38.

chunks.title: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News
chunks.text: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News THURS, OCT 22, 2026 · MIAMI, FL · 75° Miami Community Newspaper Sponsored Content Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... This is your State Senator, Alexis Calatayud. Thank you for the honor of representing your family in Tallahassee for the last four years. As your voice in the State Senate, we are tackling the pressing challenges of reducing cost-of-living and enhancing quality of life, the real issues facing our incredibly diverse community, from Key Biscayne to Homestead.

chunks.title: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News
chunks.text: There are core American values that we all share, that bind us together. They are just common sense, like an affordable pathway for the middle class to homeownership. I work everyday to fight for our shared values in tangible ways.

chunks.title: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News
chunks.text: Addressing head-on our homeownership affordability crisis, in 2023 I created Florida’s Hometown Hero down payment assistance program, a NEW pathway for Miamians to purchase their first homes! In the last four years, I fought for $300 million in state investment for our neighbors to make the American Dream of homeownership real through $35,000 at 0% interest downpayment assistance loans to help buy their first home in Miami-Dade, sooner! More than 20,000 families statewide have purchased their first home because of the Hometown Heroes down payment assistance program.

chunks.title: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News
chunks.text: $50 MILLION IN NEW funding is available for the Hometown Heroes Housing Program on July 13th, 2026. Our program provides as a second mortgage loan up to $35,000 at 0% interest in down payment and closing cost assistance for eligible first-time homebuyers in critical professions – including EARLY LEARNING AND K-12 teachers, nurses, first responders, law enforcement, healthcare workers, and many more. Apply and join the first-time home-owning families in our community living in their new home today because of Hometown Heroes! https://www.floridahousing. org/live-local-act/hometown- heroes-program Connect To Your Customers & Grow Your Business
