chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Richard Lamondin is 38 years old. He has a four-year-old son, aging parents he supports, a mortgage in a state where insurance has nearly tripled, and hundreds of employees depending on him every two weeks. He is not running away from those challenges. He is running for office because of them — and because too many families in this district are living the same story without anyone in Tallahassee fighting for them. Right now in Florida, the basics feel impossible. Preschool costs as much as rent. Insurance premiums have nearly tripled. A million people still don’t have health coverage. Our public schools are being systematically defunded.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: These aren’t accidents. They are the result of thirty years of choices made by people who will never feel them. Richard built a company from the ground up lowering costs for families and businesses across the country. Now he’s running for Florida State Senate because this community deserves a leader with actual skin in the game — and Miami now has a choice. Too many Miami families are one illness or one prescription away from financial disaster. Richard believes health care is a right, not a privilege. And that no one should lose sleep wondering how to pay a hospital bill.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: In Congress, he’ll work across the aisle to guarantee affordable, high-quality coverage with real choice — protecting the right of anyone who likes their current plan to keep it, while ensuring every family has access to an affordable public option that lowers costs for everyone. He’ll champion legislation to cap out-of-pocket expenses, expand mental-health services, and take on drug companies that keep prices high while posting record profits. Because in the richest country on earth, no one should go bankrupt just to see a doctor or fill a prescription.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Every parent knows the cost of child care has become unmanageable — and every study shows that early education changes lives. As a dad of a three-year-old, Richard has seen firsthand how broken and expensive the system is. In Miami, child care often costs as much as rent, and he feels that strain just like so many other families do. His first legislative priority will be to build bipartisan support for affordable, accessible pre-K and child care for every family , raising early-education pay, expanding hours for parents who work nights, and treating early learning like the essential service it is. Because when every child gets a fair start, every family gets a fair shot.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Miami has become the most rent-burdened county in the nation, and young people, families, and seniors are being priced out of the communities they built and have called home their whole lives. Richard believes housing isn’t just about real estate, it’s about dignity, stability, and the ability to put down roots and build generational opportunity.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: In Congress, he’ll work to treat housing as critical infrastructure , just like roads and bridges, so federal dollars flow faster to projects that expand supply and lower costs. He’ll collaborate across the aisle to reduce red tape at HUD, improve the Housing Choice Voucher program, expand first time home buyer tax credits, and restore federal funding for flood-mitigation and resilience projects that protect homeowners and lower insurance costs. Because if our hospitality workers, teachers, and first responders can’t afford to live here, we don’t have a community — we have a crisis.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: After a lifetime of work, every American deserves peace of mind. The freedom to retire without fear of losing their savings or health care. For every senior in Miami, Social Security and Medicare aren’t handouts — they’re earned promises that must be protected and strengthened. In Congress, Richard will work to preserve and strengthen Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid , ensuring they remain fully funded and off the chopping block. He’ll support measures to protect seniors from skyrocketing prescription-drug prices, safeguard pensions , and expand home- and community-based care so older Americans can age safely and comfortably in their homes.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Because the measure of a country isn’t how it treats its wealthiest, it’s how it honors those who’ve worked a lifetime to build it. SD-38 is the number one Democratic state target seat in Florida — and the race that begins to break the corruption that has controlled Tallahassee for far too long. Richard is running against a well-funded incumbent backed by special interests who have kept that majority in place. Your contribution funds the staff, organizing, ads, and the ground operation that wins this seat. Have a question for the campaign? Want to get involved, share your story, or connect with our team?

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: We want to hear from you. Richard is running to be a senator who actually shows up — and that starts now. Reach out and someone from our team will get back to you.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate Dad. Husband. Business Owner. First-time Candidate. Richard Lamondin has never worked in government or run for office. But he’s done something Tallahassee insiders haven’t: Built a successful business in Miami from the ground up — creating jobs, helping families and companies lower their utility bills, and giving back to the community he calls home. That’s exactly why we need him in the State Senate.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Born and raised in Miami, Richard is the Co-Founder & CEO of ecofi — a company proving that sustainability can be good for both people and business. Under his leadership, ecofi became one of the fastest-growing environmental services companies in the country, earning national recognition for its innovation and impact. Conserved more than 10 billion gallons of water Prevented over 300,000 metric tons of carbon emissions Helped lower utility bills for thousands of renters nationwide

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: But the path wasn’t easy. In the early years, Richard and his brother Lawrence worked multiple jobs while building ecofi from scratch. They didn’t just manage the company — they rolled up their sleeves and did the work themselves, one installation at a time. Today, Richard’s proudest role isn’t CEO. It’s dad to his son Leo, and husband to his wife Martina, right here in Miami. Now he’s stepping up to serve — not as a career politician, but as someone who’s lived the challenges this community faces, and who knows how to get real results. Now, He’s Building a Campaign to Deliver for All of Us.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Richard Lamondin isn’t running to be a politician — he’s running because too many politicians have forgotten what real life looks like. From building a clean infrastructure company with his brother to raising a young family right here in Miami, Richard knows what it means to hustle, to worry, to hope. And to show up for others. He built something from the ground up that makes a real impact: Lowering bills, creating jobs, and helping families. Now, he’s bringing that same energy to this campaign. Grandson of a WWII veteran and Teamster. Son of a Canadian immigrant who built his way into real estate. Married to an Italian immigrant and housing nonprofit director.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Co-founded ecofi , one of the fastest-growing environmental service companies in the country. Helped save 10+ billion gallons of water and lower bills for thousands of renters. Led by example: In the early years, personally installed water-saving equipment with his brother. Serves on nonprofit boards focused on youth, equity, and mental health: Project Transforming Hope – expanding economic opportunity for underserved youth. Engage Miami – mobilizing young people into civic leadership. ADAPT Foundation – providing mental health and wellness for local youth.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Richard is a homeowner, a dad, and a husband who feels the squeeze of high housing costs, rising insurance premiums, and expensive child care — just like the rest of us.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Did you know that District 40 encompasses magnificent Miami-Dade? There is no place Ana Maria would rather call home or raise two children with her husband than South Florida. Miami-Dade is a place of opportunity, culture, entrepreneurship, and hardworking families, but too many residents are feeling squeezed by rising costs. Ana Maria’s priority has been, and will continue to be, representing residents and addressing the issues that affect everyday life. That means working to make housing more affordable, cutting taxes and fees where possible, lowering homeowner’s insurance premiums, keeping communities safe, investing in schools, and supporting a strong local economy.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: As your State Representative and State Senator, Ana Maria has supported record funding for Florida’s public school system, empowered parents to make decisions about their children’s education, and championed more affordable, accessible healthcare. She has fought to keep taxes low, reduce unnecessary regulations on small businesses, and help local employers create good-paying jobs.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: In Miami-Dade, the affordability crisis is one of the most urgent challenges facing families, seniors, renters, homeowners, and small businesses. Ana Maria is focused on practical solutions that put more money back in residents’ pockets: tax relief, property insurance reform, stronger consumer protections, responsible budgeting, and policies that make it easier to build and preserve affordable and workforce housing. Cut taxes and fees so residents can keep more of what they earn. Support small businesses by reducing unnecessary red tape,  burdensome regulations, and increasing paychecks Strengthen the local economy by helping employers create and retain good-paying jobs.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Improve Florida’s unemployment compensation system so it works when residents need it most. Use a responsible, data-driven approach to economic policy that protects both livelihoods and quality of life. Fight to reduce homeowner’s insurance premiums and bring more stability, transparency, and accountability to the property insurance market. Invest in affordable and workforce housing so teachers, nurses, first responders, service workers, young families, and seniors can continue to live in the communities they serve. Support policies that expand homeownership opportunities and protect residents from being priced out of South Florida.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Identify short-, medium-, and long-term solutions to address flooding, sea level rise, and community resilience. Protect the integrity of Miami-Dade County’s Urban Development Boundary to preserve the Everglades and safeguard this irreplaceable ecosystem for future generations. Fight unnecessary toll increases that make commuting and daily life more expensive. Protect the neighborhoods, parks, schools, and local institutions that define South Florida’s quality of life. Support law enforcement, first responders, and community-based public safety efforts. Invest in community policing and practical partnerships that build trust between residents and public safety agencies.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Support local governments that choose to expand the adoption of body cameras and other accountability tools. Increase access to high-quality, affordable healthcare. Expand telehealth options for seniors, working families, and vulnerable residents. Continue efforts to reduce the cost of prescription drugs.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: A Principled, Independent Voice for South Florida Ana Maria Rodriguez is running for re-election to the Florida State Senate. After serving one term in the Florida House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020, she successfully ran for the Florida Senate, where she has built a strong record focused on improving quality of life for South Florida families, seniors, homeowners, small businesses, and working residents. She was also elected by her peers to serve as Chair of the Miami-Dade Legislative Delegation, a leadership role she continues to hold today.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Born in Miami to Cuban parents, Ana Maria understands the value of opportunity, hard work, safe communities, and a government that respects the people it serves. Her public service has been guided by a simple priority: help residents keep more of what they earn and make South Florida a more affordable place to live, work, raise a family, and retire. As a state legislator, Ana Maria has worked on issues that directly affect household budgets. She has supported keeping taxes low, reducing unnecessary burdens on small businesses, and strengthening Florida’s economy so employers can create good-paying jobs.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Ana Maria is especially focused on the affordability crisis facing South Florida. Rising costs are putting pressure on families, seniors, renters, homeowners, and small businesses – she is committed to cutting taxes, opposing unnecessary cost increases, expanding access to affordable and workforce housing, and fighting for real solutions to reduce homeowners’ insurance premiums. As the mother of school-age children, Ana Maria knows that strong schools are essential to strong communities. She has supported record funding for Florida’s public school system, as well as policies that empower parents to make the best decisions for their children’s education.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: She has spent her career advocating on behalf of the people of South Florida, both as a professional and as a public servant. Prior to being elected to the State House, she served on the Doral City Council for eight years and previously worked as the Director of Government and Community Relations for Baptist Health. Currently, she serves as Vice President of the MIAMI Association of REALTORS®, where she advocates for policies that increase homeownership, make housing more affordable, and strengthen community resilience.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: In her spare time, Ana Maria is active in the South Florida community. She has served on the Florida International University President’s Council, as the Honorary Chair of the Autism Speaks Miami Walk, and as a board member for multiple community and philanthropic organizations, including the Coral Gables Community Foundation, the City of Doral Parks & Police 4 Kids advisory board, and the Miami Lighthouse for the Blind organization’s Young Professionals of the Lighthouse Group.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Ana Maria is a proud Miami native. She attended St. Theresa Catholic School, graduated from Our Lady of Lourdes Academy, earned a B.S. in Communications from Florida International University, and earned an M.S. in Leadership from the Huizenga School of Business at Nova Southeastern University. Her husband, Dr. Clemente Canabal, is a native of Cartagena, Colombia. They live in Miami-Dade County with their two sons, Hermes and Eros.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez Miami-Dade County stay safe this Hurricane Season by being prepared! Hurricanes can happen quickly, and families may be separated. Create a plan now so everyone knows how to stay safe, communicate, and reunite after the storm. Phone numbers of a pre-assigned contact person for family members to call. List and contact information of family members, friends, neighbors and physicians. A safe place to store important documents in a waterproof container or bag. How you will get assistance if needed for older adults or those with functional needs in the home. How to turn off the water, gas and electricity safely.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Prepare an emergency supply kit with essentials your family may need during or after a storm. Keep everything in one safe place and make sure all family members know where to find it. Keep loose items in airtight plastic bags. Gather the kit’s items in easy-to-carry containers or duffel bags. Put them within reach, near the exit you use most often. Check and update your kit at least once a year. Your hurricane supply kit should contain: 7-day supply of water (one gallon per person per day, including pets) Battery-powered portable television or radio with extra batteries

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Sanitation and hygiene items, such as instant hand sanitizing gel, disinfectant wipes, moist towelettes, toilet paper, and feminine hygiene products Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), such as masks and gloves Kitchen accessories and cooking utensils Extra clothing, blankets and sleeping bags Photocopies of identification, insurance, prescriptions, household inventory, credit cards and your utility bill Copies of important documents such as birth certificates, adoption certificates, marriage licenses, divorce papers, Social Security cards, passport, green cards, will, insurance policies (home, auto, life, health, etc.), bank statements

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Prescription medications, eyeglasses, contact lens solution and hearing aid Telephone that is not dependent on electricity and/or a cell phone Formula, baby food, diapers and pacifiers Pet carriers, leashes, shot records, and food for each animal evacuating with you As you prepare for a storm, don’t forget to include your pets in your emergency plans. If you stay with family, friends, or neighbors, make sure your pets go with you.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: If you stay home during a storm, keep your family and pets together in a safe area. Use a crate or carrier for your pet, keep their collar and ID tag on, and consider microchipping them in case you become separated. If you live in an evacuation zone, mobile home, or unsafe structure, go to a pet-friendly evacuation center. During emergencies, Animal Services operates pet-friendly evacuation shelters. No pre-registration is needed, and shelter information will be shared as necessary. For everyone’s safety, pets will be evaluated by a licensed veterinarian before admission. Miami-Dade County Residents: Click here for more information.

chunks.title: Ana Maria Rodriguez – Elect Ana Maria
chunks.text: Focused on Families, Affordability, and Results . Ana Maria Rodriguez has spent her career advocating for the people of South Florida as a public servant, community leader, and working mother. She is focused on the issues families talk about around the kitchen table every day: making life more affordable, cutting taxes, lowering homeowner’s insurance premiums, improving schools, expanding access to quality healthcare, and protecting the communities that make Miami-Dade County and Monroe County special.

chunks.title: Ana Maria Rodriguez – Elect Ana Maria
chunks.text: Ana Maria believes South Florida’s best days are ahead, and she is committed to working across communities to improve the quality of life, strengthen the economy, and put more money back in the pockets of residents. Celebrating Arbor Day by giving back to the environment, one tree at a time! Great morning supporting those in need in our community at the Farm Share food distribution alongside family, friends and esteemed colleagues. Proud to be an active supporter of initiatives that encourage efficient government, informed public policy, and long-term economic growth for Florida families.

chunks.title: Jose Stoute for Florida State Senate District 40
chunks.text: Jose Stoute for Florida State Senate District 40 A voice for our community. A leader who understands service, healthcare, veterans, working families, and the future of Florida. His campaign is rooted in practical leadership, public service, and a commitment to making Florida work for families, seniors, veterans, students, and small businesses. Build an inclusive Florida where every family, senior, student, veteran, and worker has a fair chance to thrive.

chunks.title: Scott Jewett for Florida Governor - Libertarian Party
chunks.text: Scott Jewett for Florida Governor - Libertarian Party Scott Jewett will make Florida affordable. Libertarian Candidate for Florida Governor Scott Jewett is a leader, entrepreneur, innovator, lifelong problem solver, and family man who calls Boca Raton home. Like so many Floridians, he and his wife Regina face the daily realities of homeownership, rising insurance costs , and the desire to leave a freer, more prosperous state to the next generation. He is running for Governor because he believes Florida can do better , with less government overreach, more individual liberty, and practical solutions that put people first.

chunks.title: Scott Jewett for Florida Governor - Libertarian Party
chunks.text: His agenda centers on a robust economy with more living wage jobs , real educational choice, public safety, lower taxes, and a government that respects the rights of every Floridian, regardless of which major party they usually vote for. Chip in today to help power a grassroots movement that is fighting for every Floridian.

chunks.title: Scott Jewett for Florida Governor - Libertarian Party
chunks.text: Floridians are feeling the squeeze every month . Insurance premiums keep climbing, everyday costs keep rising, and too much of your hard earned money disappears into government waste. Scott Jewett is fighting to fix the insurance affordability crisis, cut taxes, shrink the size of government, and put real solutions in place that help families keep more of what they earn. He believes Florida can do better when we put people first . Libertarian Candidate for Florida Lieutenant Governor Nicole Skelly lives in Milton, Florida with her husband and their two children. Together they have owned and run a construction business for many years.

chunks.title: Scott Jewett for Florida Governor - Libertarian Party
chunks.text: As a small business owner and mom, Nicole knows the daily pressure of rising costs, heavy rules, and government overreach . She believes parents and hardworking families should be trusted more than bureaucrats. Nicole is ready to help cut the red tape that drives up prices, protect parental rights , and fight for a Florida where people can keep more of what they earn and live free. She wants her kids, and every Florida family, to have the same chance that hard work should still provide. Join the team that’s fighting for liberty in Florida. Help us knock doors, make calls, and spread the message that real change is possible. Every hour counts.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor As proposed by the Platform Committee for the Libertarian Party of Florida Annual Business Meeting of February 26th, 2022 _________________________________________ We, the Libertarian Party of Florida, oppose the initiation of force to achieve political or social goals.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We, the Libertarian Party of Florida, stand for freedom and prosperity in our State based on the principles of personal responsibility and individual liberty. We challenge the cult of the omnipotent State in order to defend and promote liberty, whereby mankind may best prosper. Libertarians seek a society built on the pillars of individual liberty and equality under the law—a society in which all individuals are sovereign over their own lives. This most desirable method of organizing society is the natural order that arises when the inalienable rights of individuals to life, liberty, and property ownership are respected and protected.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Individuals must be free to pursue their own interests and pleasures so long as their efforts do not involve the use of force or fraud, or violate the natural rights of others. Libertarians welcome the peace, prosperity, and diversity that freedom brings. In the absence of a declaration of war by the United States Congress, we oppose deployment of federal troops on Florida soil, except to defend our State in the event of foreign attack. We oppose sending Florida National Guard troops overseas. We call for restoring gubernatorial approval for the President to activate a State National Guard.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support the unfettered ability to possess, carry, and modify weapons and accessories for purposes including but not limited to self defense and to secure the rights of the free individual. We support open carry and constitutional carry initiatives in Florida. We oppose all restrictions on weapons, ammunition and accessories, unless mandated by private property owners on their premises. 3. Undelegated Powers Belong to the States or the People

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support the Tenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which reserves to the States and the people thereof all powers not expressly delegated to the federal government, nor prohibited to the States elsewhere in the Constitution. We urge the Supreme Court to overturn Wickard v. Filburn, as this act is used to nullify the Tenth Amendment by expanding federal regulatory powers over the States.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support equality under the law and condemn any law that either rewards or punishes any individual based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other group identification. Each person has the same inalienable rights. It is the State’s duty to protect those rights for everyone equally.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We recognize private property rights as an extension of self ownership, the most basic human right. One of the functions of government is to protect the rights of all people in its jurisdiction. This includes private entities having the right to voluntarily transfer ownership of their private property free of government price or quantity controls, intervention, or taxation. We support a systematic review and sunsetting of laws, regulations, and administrative guidance that do not meet the stated intent of the of the elected officials at the time of writing.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Agents of the State should not be above the law. We advocate ending the immunity of all government officials, employees, and departments, from suits for compensatory damages. We oppose caps on restitution payments. We support the Florida Whistleblower Act and the Florida False Claims Act. We support transparency and believe that Sunshine laws should apply to all public employees wherever and however they meet. All meetings and minutes must be readily available to the public and recording devices should be welcomed. There should be no laws prohibiting or limiting electronic recording devices and reporting of any public official, including law enforcement, while performing their duties.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We oppose the participation by the State of Florida in the federal Real ID Act and similar federal identification or database mandates designed to collect or share data on individuals not accused of crime. We believe in the right to privacy for all peaceful individuals and condemn any attempts to subvert this right. Detaining, searching, or seizing persons or their property should always require a warrant from a State or Federal court based on probable cause of a crime being committed.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Government should never protect, maintain, nor regulate the legal monopoly status of any corporation whether public or private, or of those corporations' ownership of any company or business. These actions create an unfair playing field and are beyond the scope of small and limited government. We believe all services, especially utilities, should operate in a free and highly competitive market, whereby benefit to the consumer is raised and costs are lowered.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We call for an end to federal spending on grants to States and local governments, coupled with an equal reduction of federal taxes. All public projects should be funded locally. Persons living and working in Florida should not be responsible financially for non federal services to citizens in a different State.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We believe marriage is a private contract between consenting adults. As such, government need not be involved in authentication, documentation, or limitation of the institution. We support abolishing licensing requirements and restrictions, recognizing these as undue burdens upon individuals and their personal lives. We favor written and witnessed prenuptial agreements to determine the dissolution process in the event of death or desired separation.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: There shall be no restrictions to the organization and mobilization of the population. This includes unrestricted ability by the whole of the people to obtain weapons, training, or supplies to defend the territory of Florida in order to secure a free and prosperous future for Floridians. 15. Immigration Law Enforcement By State and Local Governments We oppose all policies or programs that enlist State and local government employees to enforce federal immigration laws or that require local and State authorities to comply with federal immigration law enforcement. 1. State Regulation of Political Parties

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: The only electoral duty of the State government should be providing for fair and efficient conduct of elections. Political parties, like any private voluntary group, should be free from government control and allowed to establish their own rules for nomination procedures and conventions. We support Ranked Choice. We oppose Top Two primaries as this disproportionately suppresses minor political party representation in the general election. We also support including the option of None Of The Above (NOTA) on all ballots. In the event that NOTA receives a plurality of votes in any election, a new election should be held for which none of the losing candidates shall be eligible.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We recognize current campaign finance laws as threats to free speech and association. We support a structure for candidates to voluntarily disclose campaign contributions. We advocate the acceptance of alternative monetary donations such as crypto currencies as campaign contributions. We also call for the repeal of caps on contributions to candidates and parties. We support amending campaign finance laws to require all candidates and political parties to provide for their own expenses with no taxpayer funding.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support open ballot access for all parties and individuals who wish to hold public office. There must be no barriers to entry for prospective political parties and candidates, including unattainable signature requirements, exorbitant fees, or other measures which limit ballot access to a political duarchy. In addition, Section 99.103 of Florida laws, which refunds 95% of the 3% candidate filing fees only to parties with a voter registration at or above 5% of the total, should be repealed.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support and encourage private adjudication of disputes by mutually acceptable arbitrators or mediators prior to utilizing the public court system. Current law unnecessarily constrains private adjudication as a first resort. The right of trial by jury must be respected in all criminal and civil cases. We support the right of jurors to (a) take notes during trials, (b) submit written questions to witnesses and the judge, (c) be provided with the judge’s instructions in writing, and (d) discuss evidence among themselves at any time.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support the right of defendants to a fully informed jury, which requires judges to instruct jurors of their authority to judge not only the facts, but also the justice of the law according to their own consciences. If a jury of peers deems a law unjust, oppressive, or inappropriately applied, it has the right and duty to acquit the defendant. We support restitution for victims of crimes or civil infractions at the expense of the perpetrators. Victims must also enjoy respect for their right to require the prosecutor to drop charges before a trial, or pardon the perpetrator after a conviction (without necessarily foregoing restitution), provided the victim is not threatened or coerced.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: No fault divorce laws are preferable to divorce laws that require assignment of fault. For mandatory personal injury insurance we oppose no fault laws and support requiring the insurance company of the driver at fault in an accident to pay any damages due those affected. We condemn seizure of assets other than for purposes of restitution after conviction of a crime as a violation of private property rights and due process. We urge our legislators to join with other States in abolishing civil asset forfeiture and pre conviction criminal asset forfeiture.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support equal treatment and oppose sexual discrimination in any judicial proceeding adjudicating a parental right, privilege or obligation concerning his or her child. The Bar Association must cease to be the official Florida organization to which all attorneys must belong. The legal profession must be opened to competition; its clients and purely private organizations should be the judges of the quality of attorney services.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Law enforcement cannot guarantee individual safety. As such, we advocate that law enforcement is not the first line of defense for individual safety, but a second line of defense intended to render assistance to those requiring it. Self protection is a personal responsibility. Individuals have the right to defend themselves and to possess the means to do so. Decreasing the self reliance of the citizenry leads to an overemphasis of policing and an increased segregation of law enforcement personnel from the people they are paid to protect. Those in law enforcement are not above the community, but members of it.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: As such, we call for the removal of qualified immunity from all agents of law enforcement. We support the separation of federal military units from law enforcement and disaster relief. Local agencies should not accept weapons, equipment, nor training from the federal military. We call for ending the use of dogs by law enforcement; this abusive practice violates the right to privacy by performing unwarranted and unaccountable searches, and often serves to escalate conflict.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: State prison facilities must only be used for the incarceration of individuals who have violated the natural rights of other people. Non violent criminals should not be housed at the expense of the public. Instead, non violent criminals should be kept on parole, closely monitored, limited in heir interaction with sensitive populations, and required to pay restitution to those whom they have wronged. The imprisonment of citizens should be undertaken with the strictest of scrutiny, as the incentives of prison operators and the mechanisms by which they are compensated are ripe for abuse.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We oppose the use of red light cameras as a photo enforcement tool as well as any third party non law enforcement agency issuing fines of any kind. As individuals with rights to govern ourselves and our property, we support the ability to extend those rights to private security firms for the purposes of defending our life, liberty, and property. The power of arrest should be reserved to county sheriffs and their assigns. Outside agencies should be required to obtain permission from the sheriff prior to acting in the sheriff's jurisdiction. We oppose law enforcement “quotas” of any kind as a requirement or incentive in any law enforcement agency or activities.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We oppose acceptance of federal funds by the State of Florida, or agencies thereof, which are earmarked for continuing the War on Drugs. Police roadblocks, Rights Free Zones, and searches without probable cause should be abolished. This includes U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s 100 Mile Border Zone which covers our State in its entirety. 11. Pandemics and other Force Majeure Events

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Government must never overstep its bounds, even in response to force majeure events, which include pandemics, natural disasters, and other crises. We condemn any misuse of authority by government to limit or restrict the rights of private property owners. We oppose all government restrictions on the transfer of information related to the event.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Criminal sentencing should be reserved for crimes which have a discernible victim. The punishment should be appropriate to the crime. We oppose all laws and regulations that attempt to protect individuals from the consequences of their own behavior. While not necessarily condoning such activities, we advocate the repeal of all laws criminalizing gambling, possession and sale of drugs, and sexual relations between consenting adults. All those presently incarcerated or ever convicted solely for the commission of these victimless crimes must be pardoned and their records expunged. 2. Prohibitions by Private Organizations

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Private voluntary organizations, such as communities, clubs, unions, private universities or businesses may enforce rules that prohibit certain activities, such as gambling, prostitution, drug free or smoke free dorms. We advocate voluntary means of raising government revenues, such as user fees and donations, rather than taxation backed by force or threat of force. So long as citizens are coerced into funding government, we believe that government should accept payment in kind, in commodities, or in non fiat currencies.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: The State of Florida has levied enough taxes on its citizens and trade partners, as such, no new taxes ought to be levied for new government projects. New projects must be funded from existing revenues by reducing inefficiencies or cutting current spending.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: As long as we have taxes, equal protection of the law requires that for each type of tax, the rates should be the same and the tax base should be calculated in the same way for every individual or business. There should be no abatements, subsidies, credits, refunds or other preferential treatments as incentives to businesses to invest or create jobs, or as a privilege to individuals or classes of individuals, such as age, race or location. Such tax favoritism should be unconstitutional.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Legislative budgeting of government has historically failed to control spending or the size of government. Therefore, we support amending the State Constitution to require a supermajority of the legislative houses to approve a total budget that exceeds that of the previous year and annual auditing of all funds spent made available by request as well as posted on State websites. In support of Localism, we prefer home rule as it is the most local jurisdiction of government, over ones more removed in State or Federal, as these entities largely consist of legislators from other jurisdictions.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support free markets. We oppose all government laws or regulations, including but not limited to controls on prices, wages, rent, amounts sold, employment terms, ownership share terms, or other contractual terms, which interfere with private voluntary transactions. Ownership of property includes the right to transfer that property on any terms acceptable to all parties involved. 2. Alternative Currencies and Legal Tender The State shall not impose any regulations or restrictions on alternative currencies to the U.S. Dollar, nor shall it enforce legal tender laws.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We reject favoritism in any form to any industries, companies or other organizations. We oppose all grants, loans, loan guarantees and investments in business by any State or local government and all regulatory schemes that create privileges or disadvantages to any business or industry. We call for abolishing all business and occupational licenses. The right of the people to conduct commerce is inherent, and should not require the permission of the State.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support the right of private parties to provide charity and aid to those in need, and applaud court rulings correctly affirming First Amendment protection for that right. We condemn any effort by government to curtail or restrict private charity, and call for replacing government organizations and agencies which currently offer such aid and assistance with voluntary private efforts. 1. Parental Responsibility and Choice of Schools

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Because parents or guardians are best situated to decide what is in their own children’s best interests, it should be their right to decide their choice of school, type of school organization or homeschooling for them, and the responsibility of no one else to pay for it. Since the ultimate responsibility for the education of children rests with their parents, compulsory schooling and truancy laws must be repealed. 2. Civil Liberties in Government Education

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We oppose random drug tests and locker searches without probable cause, censorship of student publications or speeches, disarming of adults, school promotion of religion, suppression of student religious expressions, and other restrictions of civil liberties in government run schools . 1. Measures to Prevent Environmental Damage

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Protecting the environment requires a clear definition and enforcement of individual rights and responsibilities regarding resources like land, water, air, and wildlife. Oceans and waterways may not be deeded lands, but are to be protected and conserved similarly. Where damages can be proven and quantified in a court of law, restitution to the injured parties must be required. Immunity shall not be given to any industry, processor, or individual, related to damages occurring through these mediums, such as chemical run off. Other unowned mediums such as air, radio frequency, light, and sound should also be treated similarly when damages occur.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Civil remedies are best pursued to make whole any victims. We look forward to the day when all property not required for police and court functions are returned to private ownership and control. Privatization of all public land not critical to government operations, may deed lock its future use for conservation or commercialization. We oppose the creation of new government parks or wilderness and recreation areas. Such parks and areas that already exist should be transferred to non government ownership. Pending such transfer, their operating costs should be borne by their users rather than by taxpayers. 3. State Withholding of Clean Energy Technology

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: The withholding or prohibition of clean energy technologies by any government, military, or public entity, is viewed as equal to racketeering, and we oppose such manipulation of markets and such secrecy. The most fundamental property right is an individual’s right to own and control his or her own body. All individuals have the right to determine their own healthcare needs and treatment. Government should neither interfere nor impose upon the practitioner patient relationship. The right of people to extend or end their lives with dignity should not be infringed. We support the freedom to use living wills and durable medical powers of attorney.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We support free choice for healthcare services, products and procedures, including the right to use experimental treatments. We favor free market regulation for all healthcare related matters, such as medication, providers, hospitals, insurance, testing, and the advocacy of same. 5. Medical Boards, Standards and Equipment We support voluntary medical boards and the free market establishment of industry standards and practices, and oppose government created barriers to entry. The manufacture of medication and medical equipment should not require approval by government.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: We recognize secession as a political right that sovereigns reserve to sever any relationship which they voluntarily enter. The exercise of this right should not eliminate any legal or moral obligations to uphold the rights of others, including any debts owed. We recognize and affirm that the sovereign State of Florida is in a voluntary relationship with the Union of States, and the sovereign individual is in a voluntary relationship with the State of Florida. We favor these entities, as they see fit, having regular and deliberative debate discerning the state of their union between them and larger bodies of government.

chunks.title: Platform | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: The Libertarian Party of Florida ratifies and hereby includes in this document the platform of the national Libertarian Party. Our silence about any other particular government law, regulation, ordinance, directive, edict, control, restriction, regulatory agency, activity, or objections should not be construed to imply approval. Chip in today to help power a grassroots movement that is fighting for every Floridian. The Libertarian Party of Florida says you own your life. We agree. We will uphold and defend the Constitution, not just talk about it during campaign season. This campaign is for every Floridian. The smallest minority is the individual. That is who we serve.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor Florida families are paying more and getting less Florida does not have one money problem. It has a stack of them . Insurance. Taxes. Housing. Power bills. Healthcare. Government growth. They all land on the same kitchen table. Scott Jewett and Nicole Skelly trust you. You know how to raise your kids, run your shop, and take care of your family. You should keep more of what you earn . You should live free. Scroll down to get more information about where we stand on the issues and what we plan to do. You can also click on one of the issues from the list to go directly to that issue . Scroll Down or Select an Issue From the List!

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: AI Data Centers & Florida’s Energy Future We have an affordability crisis. Groceries, housing, homeowners insurance, property taxes, utilities, gas, car insurance, car payments, health insurance, childcare, and eating out are more expensive now. Utilities keep climbing. Parents pick up extra hours. Gig workers drive later. Small shops stay open longer and still fall behind. Government did not feel that squeeze first. Families did. When Tallahassee or Washington adds a rule, a fee, or a new program, the cost shows up in the price of milk, the rent check, and the mortgage payment on a modest home.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Floridians are not asking for a lecture about the economy. They are asking why they work harder and keep less. Hardworking people should keep more of what they earn. Government should get out of the way so prices can come down and paychecks can stretch further. Cost of living is not one bill. It is insurance, property taxes, housing, energy, healthcare, and red tape stacked on the same family. Fix those pressures and everyday life gets cheaper. We trust Floridians to run their own budgets . Government should have to live on one too. Treat cost of living as the test for every state decision: does this make life cheaper for families, or more expensive?

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Cut rules and fees that raise the price of food, housing, energy, insurance, and hiring. Stop shifting government costs onto household bills. Force agencies to show how new rules hit parents, retirees, renters, and small shops before those rules take effect. Tie the rest of this agenda together — insurance, taxes, housing, healthcare, energy, and spending — so the kitchen table squeeze actually eases. Florida families should not have to work two jobs to afford one life. Keep what you earn. Live free. Florida homeowners pay some of the highest premiums in the country . When the roof leaks or the storm hits, too little of that money comes back to fix the house.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Retirees on fixed incomes open a renewal letter and wonder if they can stay. Young families trying to buy a first home get priced out before they ever unpack. Small landlords raise rent because the premium jumped again. Coastal towns watch private insurers leave, then watch Citizens grow. The system is broken by waste, lawsuits that do not help homeowners, rules that chase companies out, and claims practices that grind families down. Storm risk is real. The bloated system on top of that risk is a choice. Floridians are not asking for another press conference. They are asking why they pay six times more in premiums than they ever see paid out in claims.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Insurance should protect the home, not feed a bloated system . Premiums should be honest. Claims should get paid. Families should not be trapped with one expensive option. Homeowners deserve competition, clear rules, and a market that wants to write coverage in Florida . Citizens should be a safety net, not the default company for half the state. Scott has already drafted insurance reform work because he refuses to accept that this is “just Florida.” People who pay the bill deserve a system that works when they need it. Cut the waste that drives premiums up and keeps claim dollars from reaching damaged homes. Increase competition so more companies want to insure Florida families.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Protect homeowners from abusive claims practices and endless runaround. Keep Citizens as a backstop, not a growing substitute for a working market. Tell families the truth about flood risk and storm exposure instead of hiding costs until renewal day. Measure reform the only way that matters: are premiums coming down, and do claims get paid? Your home should not be a luxury item because the insurance system failed. Fix the insurance affordability crisis. You worked a lifetime to own your house. Then the county sends another bill for the privilege of living in it. If the value on paper goes up, the tax can go up even when your paycheck does not.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: That hits retirees on fixed incomes first. It hits widows who want to stay on the same street. It hits young families who finally bought a starter home and then learned the tax bill is another mortgage. Parents should not have to choose between keeping the house and paying for groceries. Small shops tied to a building feel the same squeeze. Local government got used to spending the increase. Families got used to being told there is no other way. There is another way. If you own your home, you should not keep paying rent to the government forever. Eliminate 100% of property taxes on homesteaded homes . Your home, your money, and your freedom belong to you, not them.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Florida families should never be taxed out of houses they already paid for . Government should live within its means, just like those families do. Property tax relief is not a gift . It is the state admitting it does not own your house. Fight to eliminate homestead property taxes so owners are not billed every year for staying in their own home. Force state and local governments to set priorities and cut waste instead of leaning on the next assessment increase. Protect retirees and fixed income owners who did everything right and still fear the tax notice. Be honest that government will have to spend less. That is the point. Families already do.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: If you own your home, you shouldn’t have to keep paying the government for the privilege of living in it. Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive A young couple wants a starter home near work. The listing is gone in a weekend, or the payment is impossible once insurance and taxes land on top of the mortgage . A teacher rents farther from school each year. A restaurant crew drives an hour because nothing nearby is open at their wage. That is not only a market story. Rules, delays, and layered approvals make it slower and more expensive to build the homes working people need. When government makes building hard, families pay rent for the delay.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Longtime residents get pushed out of the neighborhoods they helped build . Adult children cannot move back near their parents. Small landlords sell because insurance and taxes ate the margin. “Affordable housing” becomes a slogan while the starter home disappears. Floridians should not have to leave Florida to afford Florida. Housing gets cheaper when people are free to build, buy, and rent without a maze of permission . Get government out of the way of new homes, especially starter homes. Property rights matter . So does the ability of working people to live near the jobs that keep this state running. We will not pretend a new office in Tallahassee can wish prices down . Cut the barriers.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Strip the red tape that makes ordinary homes take years and extra dollars to approve. Support local decisions that add starter homes and rentals without turning every project into a political fight. Stop stacking insurance, tax, and fee costs onto the monthly payment until working families are priced out. Respect property rights while rejecting the idea that government should pick winners among developers. Measure success by whether nurses, teachers, tradespeople, and young families can still live in their communities. Florida should be a place you can start a life, not a place you get priced out of.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: A free country should welcome peaceful people who come here to work, build a life, and join a community . Freedom also depends on knowing who is coming in. When the system is slow, confusing, and unfair, honest people wait in line while criminals, traffickers, and cartels look for gaps . That is not compassion. That is a broken process that hurts citizens, legal immigrants, workers, and business owners. Florida families feel it in crowded services, strained schools, and job sites where the rules seem to apply to some people and not others . Small business owners who follow the law watch competitors who do not. Communities want order, not chaos and not cruelty.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: The two major parties use this issue to raise money and pick a fight . Floridians want a system that is lawful, faster for honest people, and tough on people who hurt others. Secure the border. Make legal immigration simpler and faster . Focus enforcement on criminals, traffickers, and real security threats. Peaceful people who want to work and follow the law should not face a wall of bureaucracy . People who commit crimes should not get a pass. The goal is more freedom, less bureaucracy , and a system that is fair to citizens, immigrants, workers, and businesses alike. Support secure borders and clear enforcement against criminals, traffickers, and genuine security threats.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Push for a simpler, faster legal path so honest people can come, work, and contribute without disappearing into a backlog. Stop using Floridians as props in a national shouting match. Protect the rule of law so legal residents and citizens are not asked to ignore the rules everyone else is told to follow. Judge policy by whether communities are safer and whether peaceful workers have a lawful way in. Welcome people who come to build a life and assimilate. Stop people who come to harm our way of life. Make the lawful path the easier path. Parents know their children better than any official in Tallahassee. They know how their kid learns. They know when a school is working and when it is not.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Too often the system protects itself first . Families get assigned a building and told to be grateful. Teachers get buried in paperwork. Kids who need something different wait. A mom who wants to homeschool, pick a charter, or try a small private school should not have to fight the state for permission to do what is best for her child. Young people starting out need skills that lead to work , not a pile of debt and a diploma that does not open a door. Higher education should serve students, not a bureaucracy. Education is not a turf war between politicians . It is a parent standing in a doorway asking, “Will this help my kid?”

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Parents decide. Funding should follow the student , whether that is a traditional public school, a charter, a private school, homeschool, or another option that fits the child. ZIP code and income should not trap a family in a school that is failing their kid . Choice is for every parent, not only the ones who can already buy their way out. Education should help children succeed. It should not exist to protect a government system. Put parents in the driver’s seat and keep them there. Make money follow the child so families have real options, not just a brochure. Cut the rules that bury teachers in paperwork and pull time away from students.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Keep curriculum decisions close to families. No identity politics in the classroom. Teach kids. Don’t recruit them. Demand results from schools and colleges that take public money. If it does not help students, it does not get a blank check. Parents, not bureaucrats, should make the big choices for their kids. Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use. Healthcare is personal. It is the nurse on a long shift who still cannot afford her own bill. It is the family opening a surprise statement after a short ER visit. It is the worker who loses a job and suddenly wonders if the medicine stays available.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: This year, hundreds of thousands of Floridians lost subsidized coverage or saw prices jump. People did not become less sick. The paperwork and the price tag changed. Government keeps adding rules that sound helpful and then show up as higher premiums, narrower networks, and fewer choices . Small business owners trying to cover a crew feel it. Gig workers who buy their own plan feel it. Retirees stuck between systems feel it. Families do not need another slogan. They need a doctor they can see and a bill they can pay. Patients and healthcare professionals should come first. People need affordable care and more choices, not a thicker rulebook.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Government should not make healthcare more expensive or more confusing . More options, clearer prices, and fewer barriers beat another layer of control. A nurse or doctor should be free to care for patients. A family should be free to pick the coverage that fits their life. Fight rules that raise premiums and shrink the number of plans families can actually use. Push for clearer prices so a parent can know the cost before the bill arrives. Expand choices for workers, small shops, and people who buy coverage on their own. Keep the focus on patients and the people who treat them, not on protecting a system.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Tell the truth when federal subsidy changes hit Florida households, and refuse to pretend Tallahassee can hide the cost. People need care they can reach and a price they can live with. Government should stop making that harder. Florida is growing because people want to be here. That should be good news. Too often it feels like a traffic jam, a crowded classroom, and a construction fence where a familiar view used to be. Parents spend half the afternoon in the car. Truck drivers lose hours on the same stretch of road. Homeowners watch a wetland or a tree line vanish and then get told the pipes and schools will “catch up later.” Later usually means another fee.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Growth without capacity is how you get angry neighborhoods and brittle systems . Growth with a pile of special deals is how you get the feeling that someone else got the break. People are not against the next family moving in. They are against a government that approves the rooftops and forgets the roads, water, and schools those rooftops need. Communities should grow without being crushed . Infrastructure is not a favor. If you allow the houses, you have to be honest about the roads, water, sewer, and classrooms. Local people and property owners should have a real voice . Distant agencies and sweetheart incentives should not run the map.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Florida can welcome people and still protect the places that make this state worth living in. Demand that roads, water, sewer, and schools keep up with growth instead of trailing it by a decade. Cut the delays that raise costs, then dump those costs on the next buyer. Stop using taxpayer incentives to force growth the community cannot support. Respect property rights and local voices when a project changes a neighborhood. Be honest about tradeoffs. Growth is not free. Neither is pretending the pipes will appear on their own. Florida can grow and still feel like home. The roads, water, and schools have to keep up, and the special deals have to stop.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Chip in today to help power a grassroots movement that is fighting for every Floridian. Hurricanes, Flooding, Water & Environmental Protection A family that just finished boarding the windows should not also be praying the insurance company picks up the phone . A fisherman knows the water. A farmer knows the land. A homeowner on a canal knows what happens when the surge comes.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Florida lives with storms. That will not change. What can change is whether we keep building the next neighborhood in the next vulnerable place, then acting surprised when the bill arrives. Water quality, the Everglades, and coastal flooding are not abstract “environment” talk. They are drinking water, jobs, and whether the house is still standing. FAU polling found most Floridians worry about stronger storms and worse surge. They are right to. Risk is real. Hiding it until premium day is how families get trapped. Good stewards already live here . They do not need a lecture from a distant agency.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: They need honest rules, working mitigation , and a government that does not make recovery harder than the storm. Farmers, fishermen, and homeowners care for the land they live on . Good stewards, not distant agencies, should make the big decisions about their own property. Protecting water and coast is how you protect homes, jobs, and the next generation’s Florida . Property rights and clean water are not opposites. Storm readiness and insurance costs are the same conversation . Pretending otherwise is how premiums explode after the season ends. Support preparedness and mitigation that actually protect homes and businesses, not just press releases after landfall.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Be honest about flood and surge risk so families are not sold a house the system cannot insure. Protect water quality and the Everglades without burying working people in paperwork that does not clean a single gallon. Respect property rights. Stop treating every owner like the problem. Connect storm policy to insurance reform so recovery does not become a second disaster. Protect the home. Protect the water. Trust the people who live on the land to be good stewards of it. Government Spending, Taxes & Accountability

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: When a family earns less, they cut what they cannot afford . When a small shop has a bad month, the owner skips a draw and watches every receipt. Government does the opposite. It asks for more. Floridians see waste and then get told the answer is another tax, another fee, another program . Retirees who saved carefully watch Tallahassee spend like the well never runs dry. Parents who pack lunches watch agencies grow. Rules pile up. So do hidden costs. A new form does not look like a tax . It still takes a Saturday the shop owner does not have. A camera network does not look like a tax. It still treats free people like suspects for driving to work.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Accountability is not a slogan. It is whether anyone can follow the money and say no. It is your money . Government should spend it only when the expense is truly necessary. Lower taxes and tighter budgets force government to set priorities, cut waste, and become accountable. That is how families already live. Transparency is not optional . Free people have a right to see how they are being governed — and a right not to be tracked just for using the road. Demand that government live on a budget the way families and small shops already do. Cut waste before asking taxpayers for another dollar. Shrink the rulebook that costs time and money without making life safer or better.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Open the books. If the public cannot see it, it should not be spent. Oppose warrantless tracking of everyday Floridians, including ALPR and Flock style camera networks that log parents, nurses, and delivery drivers. Stop asking taxpayers for more. Start making government do more with what it already has. Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights. A store owner should not dread the next smash and grab . A parent should not change the walk to school. A senior living alone should not feel like the easy target. Nurses leaving a night shift should get to the car in peace. "Teen Take Overs" are not an acceptable trend.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Florida communities need to be safe . That means going after people who hurt others: violent offenders, traffickers, dealers who poison neighborhoods, and crews that treat theft like a business. It also means the justice system should spend its time on real threats, not on turning everyday life into a dragnet . Warrantless cameras that log every errand do not make a family safer. They treat free people like suspects. Law abiding parents and homeowners have the right to protect their families . Public safety and constitutional rights are not a trade. A free state can do both.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Keep communities safe . Give law enforcement the tools to go after violent crime, trafficking, drugs, and organized theft. Demand accountability . Focus the justice system on people who pose a real threat. Protect the rights of everyone else. Free people should not have their every move recorded for driving down the road . This campaign opposes ALPR camera networks and mass surveillance of lawful residents. Law abiding Floridians have the right to keep and bear arms to protect their homes and families . That right should not be chipped away by politicians who do not trust the people. Support effective policing aimed at violent crime, trafficking, drugs, and organized theft.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Push courts and prosecutors to focus resources on people who threaten public safety. Protect constitutional rights, including due process and the right of law abiding people to defend themselves. Reject mass surveillance of everyday travel, including Flock style ALPR systems. Give local law enforcement flexibility to solve problems in their own communities, and hold them accountable when they abuse that power. Safe streets. Free people. Go after real threats. Leave law abiding Floridians alone.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Nicole and her husband have made payroll since 2007. They know what a new rule from Tallahassee does to a small carpentry shop . It does not hit the politician first. It hits the owner who cannot pass the cost on and the crew that needs hours next week. Gig workers picking up weekend rides, parents running a side hustle from the kitchen table, and young people trying to start something all run into the same wall : permits, licenses, and delays that have nothing to do with serving a customer.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Florida can attract new industries . It can also scare them off with taxes, power bill surprises, and a rulebook that only the big players can afford to read. Workers do not need a slogan about jobs. They need an employer who can afford to hire them. A robust economy with more living wage work is how families stay . Government does not create that by adding another office. It creates that by getting out of the way. Trust people who build things . Small shops, the self employed, and gig workers should be free to earn a living without asking permission for every step.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Keep taxes competitive. Cut rules that make it expensive to hire. Welcome new industries without handing them a taxpayer subsidy. Scott has built companies and solved hard problems in the private sector . Nicole has kept a family business alive through good years and bad ones. That is the economy they will fight for. Cut occupational licenses and rules that block people from working. Make it cheaper and simpler to hire, especially for small shops. Keep Florida competitive on taxes without selling the state off through special deals. Support workforce paths that lead to real jobs, trades, skills, and new industries, instead of paperwork theaters.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Say no to barriers that protect connected companies and punish the next startup. Let Floridians work, hire, and build. The best jobs plan is less permission and more freedom. AI Data Centers & Florida’s Energy Future A potential simple solution: The data center provides its own power, uses an internal heat exchange cooling system similar to a car radiator, and is not built near neighborhoods or cities. This way they don't use existing power grids or existing water supplies. A retiree on a fixed income should not see the power bill jump because a warehouse of computers moved in down the road. A small shop should not subsidize the water and substations of a company that could write a check.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Artificial intelligence is bringing real investment. That can mean jobs and better tools. It can also mean massive data centers that gulp electricity, water, and land. When government hands out incentives and then quietly socializes the infrastructure, ordinary Floridians pick up the tab . Neighbors worry about wells, wetlands , and whether the next rate case will treat a tech campus like just another customer. Property owners worry about eminent domain dressed up as “economic development.” Parents wonder why their light bill is part of someone else’s business plan. Florida should not be for sale. Innovation is welcome. A hidden tax on households is not.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: Welcome technological investment . Do not force residents and small businesses to subsidize it. Data centers should pay their own way for power, water, land, and grid upgrades . Taxpayers should not underwrite some of the world’s largest technology companies. Energy policy should serve Florida families first . That includes cleaner, safer, reliable power, and it includes nuclear as part of a serious energy future. Property rights and local voices come before ribbon cuttings. Require data centers and similar projects to cover the power, water, and infrastructure they use instead of shifting costs onto household rates.

chunks.title: The Issues | Scott Jewett for Florida Governor
chunks.text: End taxpayer incentives that socialize the downside and privatize the upside for giant tech firms. Protect property rights and water resources when a project changes a community. Plan energy capacity for Florida homes and shops first, then for industrial demand that pays its own bill. He's running for Florida Governor because he believes Florida can do better , with less government overreach, more individual liberty, and practical solutions that put people first.

chunks.text: Family is central to how Scott sees the world: protect what matters, take responsibility, and leave things better than you found them . "I am proud to carry forward a legacy of Libertarian values passed down from my father and grandfather. Raised with a commitment to helping those in need and upholding strong ethical standards, these principles have guided me throughout my life."

chunks.text: Born in Seattle in 1959 and raised in San Diego, Scott was the kind of kid who preferred the canyons and the garage to sitting still in a classroom . At 16 he took a job as a dishwasher at a Bonanza Steakhouse; by 18 he was in management. The carpet cleaning business he launched with a partner in those early years is still operating today.
