chunks.title: Jose Javier Rodriguez
chunks.text: Jose Javier Rodriguez Launches Campaign for Florida Attorney General Vows to take on corruption and high prices, and serve as the People’s Lawyer MIAMI, FL.-  Today, workers’ rights attorney and former State Senator Jose Javier Rodriguez officially launched his campaign for Florida Attorney General, committing to fight corruption and special interests, and protect everyday Floridians from fraud and high prices. A lifelong champion for working families, Rodriguez has spent his career standing up to powerful interests and holding bad actors accountable.

chunks.title: Jose Javier Rodriguez
chunks.text: “For decades, powerful interests have rigged the system to serve themselves while everyday working Floridians are left paying more but getting less,” said Jose Javier Rodriguez . “I’m running to be the People’s Lawyer to keep us safe, root out corruption, and go after those who make backroom deals in Tallahassee to pass costs onto us; I’m running to give families, workers and homeowners some relief.”

chunks.title: Jose Javier Rodriguez
chunks.text: I’ve never been afraid to take on tough fights, whether it’s holding powerful corporations accountable, challenging broken systems, or defending everyday Floridians. The law should protect people, not the powerful. So let me be clear: as the People’s Lawyer, if you’re dangerous or scamming Floridians, no matter how powerful you are, I’m coming for you.” Rodríguez brings a personal commitment to justice and American democracy. His father left communism in Cuba. Growing up in Florida, faith and community were central to the way his mother and father raised him -- and these guided his life and career.

chunks.title: Jose Javier Rodriguez
chunks.text: As an attorney, he fought for workers and homeowners in the courtroom; and as State Senator, he fought for everyday families in Tallahassee. He stood up to powerful interests, battling for-profit colleges that preyed on students and condominium associations that took advantage of homeowners. Most recently, as Assistant Secretary at the U.S. Department of Labor, he worked to expand access to good-paying jobs. His announcement comes as the Florida Republican Attorney General faces serious accusations of involvement in money laundering and wire fraud, and could be held in contempt for defying a court order.

chunks.title: Jose Javier Rodriguez
chunks.text: As Attorney General, José Javier Rodríguez will restore integrity to the office and use its full power to hold powerful interests accountable, defend our Constitution, protect vulnerable communities, and ensure justice works for everyone. chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Launches Investigation into Homeowners Insurers for Blocking Outside Claims Assistance | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: Attorney General James Uthmeier Launches Investigation into Homeowners Insurers for Blocking Outside Claims Assistance | My Florida Legal Attorney General James Uthmeier Launches Investigation into Homeowners Insurers for Blocking Outside Claims Assistance TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Attorney General James Uthmeier announced that his office has started an investigation and sent a subpoena for documents to Velocity Risk Underwriters, LLC. The investigation looks at possible illegal agreements involving insurance policy rules that stop homeowners from hiring their own licensed public adjusters.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Launches Investigation into Homeowners Insurers for Blocking Outside Claims Assistance | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: “Florida homeowners—especially those rebuilding after a hurricane—should have a fair chance to get the full value of their claim,” said Attorney General James Uthmeier . “We are looking into whether Velocity and other insurance companies worked together to ban public adjusters so they could pay out less money. Insurance companies use their own adjusters. Homeowners should be allowed to hire an advocate on their side too.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Launches Investigation into Homeowners Insurers for Blocking Outside Claims Assistance | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: Some homes are harder to insure than others—especially beachfront properties and houses with older roofs. These homes are often covered by special “surplus lines” insurance policies. After storm damage, many homeowners hire a licensed public adjuster. A public adjuster is a licensed professional who works only for the homeowner. They inspect the damage, figure out repair costs, and help the homeowner deal with the insurance company. Homeowners who use a public adjuster can receive up to 30 percent more money on their claims than those who do not.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Launches Investigation into Homeowners Insurers for Blocking Outside Claims Assistance | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: The investigation focuses on special policy rules called “anti-public adjuster” clauses. Under these rules, if a homeowner hires a public adjuster, the insurance company can reject the entire claim. Velocity writes thousands of these policies in Florida, covering millions of dollars in premiums. The subpoena demands that Velocity turn over records about its membership in trade groups, any communications with other insurance companies, and any agreements to stop homeowners from using public adjusters.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures the Return of Millions from Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company to the Florida Hurricane Catastrop
chunks.text: TALLAHASSEE, Fla.–Attorney General James Uthmeier secured the return of tens of millions of dollars from Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company (UPCIC) to the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund (FHCF). The agreement resolves allegations that the company fraudulently submitted numerous ineligible claims for reimbursement in violation of the Florida False Claims Act. This is the first time the Office of the Attorney General has secured repayment related to an insurance fraud case.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures the Return of Millions from Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company to the Florida Hurricane Catastrop
chunks.text: “Thanks to the outstanding work of Associate Deputy Attorney General Nicholas Weilhammer, Director Liz Brady, and Assistant Attorney General Andrew Butler, our office secured the return of more than $30 million to the state’s hurricane fund from fraudulent insurance submission allegations following Hurricane Irma,” said Attorney General James Uthmeier . “As Floridians, we know the impact that hurricanes can have on our state and how important recovery efforts are in a storm’s aftermath in helping residents start to rebuild. This office is committed to a healthy and stable insurance market for Florida homeowners, meaning insurance companies must play by the rules.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures the Return of Millions from Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company to the Florida Hurricane Catastrop
chunks.text: The FHCF is a tax-exempt state trust fund administered by the State Board of Administration that serves a vital role in stabilizing the Florida insurance market when hurricanes cause widespread or catastrophic damage. FHCF provides reimbursements to residential property insurance companies for a portion of their payments to homeowners for hurricane-related property damage. In the event of widespread, major hurricanes, such as Hurricane Irma, FHCF provides a backstop to the losses faced by insurance carriers.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures the Return of Millions from Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company to the Florida Hurricane Catastrop
chunks.text: Following a whistleblower lawsuit filed in Leon County, the Office of the Attorney General launched its own investigation into UPCIC to ensure that the claims submitted by the company were, in fact, caused by Hurricane Irma. During the course of that investigation, numerous unrelated claims were identified in the submissions from UPCIC to the FHCF. As a result, the company agreed not to seek reimbursement for those claims, lowering the FHCF payout from Hurricane Irma to UPCIC by more than $30 million. The company also agreed to pay more than $4 million in fines and implement changes to its policies and procedures. To view a copy of the agreement, click here .

chunks.text: TALLAHASSEE, Fla.—Attorney General James Uthmeier announced that he is sending a formal letter  to the U.S. Department of Transportation and the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration urging the federal government to revoke commercial driver’s license (CDL) program authority and strip related federal funding from California and Washington following the deadly crash on August 12th, 2025, that claimed three lives.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Requests US DOT to Revoke CDL Programs & Funding from California and Washington; Supports Agricultural and State Law E
chunks.text: “States like California and Washington ignored the rules, gave an illegal alien a license to drive a 40-ton truck, and three people are dead as a result. A preventable tragedy due to sanctuary state policies,” said Attorney General James Uthmeier. “In response, we’re supporting our Agricultural Law Enforcement and state police to ramp up inspections at state entry-points for illegal aliens who may be operating large trucks using out-of-state driver’s licenses. If you’re here illegally or can’t speak English, you have no business operating large commercial vehicles on Florida’s roads.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Requests US DOT to Revoke CDL Programs & Funding from California and Washington; Supports Agricultural and State Law E
chunks.text: We commend Commissioner Simpson and his department’s 287(g) certified law enforcement officers for turning Florida’s interdiction stations into strongholds of immigration enforcement. chunks.text: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) Commissioner Wilton Simpson made the announcement alongside Attorney General Uthmeier at an agricultural interdiction station along Interstate 10 in Live Oak. All FDACS sworn law enforcement officers were certified in July, and they are stationing at interdiction checkpoints to work together with federal and state partners on immigration enforcement and checking for English proficiency for commercial drivers  while continuing agricultural inspections.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Requests US DOT to Revoke CDL Programs & Funding from California and Washington; Supports Agricultural and State Law E
chunks.text: These interdiction stations, which are distinct from FDOT weigh stations, will serve as critical enforcement points to stop human smuggling, fraudulent documents, and unsafe commercial vehicles.

chunks.text: “The crash on the Florida Turnpike tragically took the lives of three Floridians and was a completely preventable consequence of illegal immigration and sanctuary-state policies. chunks.text: “By leveraging our agricultural inspection stations and 287(g) certified officers, we are working hand in hand with state and federal partners to identify dangerous drivers, enforce immigration laws, and combat criminal activity,” said FDACS Office of Agricultural Law Enforcement Colonel Rick “Lee” Adams Jr. “I want to thank Commissioner Wilton Simpson and Attorney General James Uthmeier for their unwavering leadership in standing up for law and order and ensuring that Florida remains a national leader in immigration enforcement.”

chunks.text: The Attorney General’s letter to the federal government cites alarming findings released by the U.S. Department of Transportation. chunks.text: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners | My Florida Legal Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners TALLAHASSEE, Fla .— Attorney General James Uthmeier announced a final judgment against MV Realty for deceiving Florida homeowners. The final ruling requires MV to remove liens from over 9,000 Florida homes and make a $3 million dollar payment by June 30, 2026. Failure to comply with the judgment entitles the state to collect the entire $18,000,000.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: “MV Realty scammed thousands of Florida homeowners, and now justice has prevailed,”  said Attorney General James Uthmeier.  “This massive legal win set the standard for other states looking to move forward with similar investigations and lawsuits against these scammers. I’d like to thank the entire Consumer Protection team for their dedication and delivering results for Floridians.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: MV Realty PBC, LLC and its principals, Antony Mitchell, Amanda Zachman, and David Manchester, bombarded financially vulnerable homeowners with deceptive offers to give the homeowners “free” nominal payments that they “would never have to repay.” In exchange for the payment, the homeowner had to agree to use MV Realty as an exclusive listing broker if they decide to sell their home.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: Hidden in the fine language of the so-called “Homeowner Benefit Agreement,” however, was a 40-year lien or encumbrance on the property that required the homeowner to pay a minimum of 3% of the home’s value to MV Realty, regardless of whether the company ever provided any listing services. These contracts put consumers over a barrel, forcing many homeowners to pay the 3% fee when they refinanced, transferred, or devised their property to heirs.  MV Realty collected unconscionable fees even if the homeowner went into foreclosure.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: The Office of the Attorney General sued MV Realty under the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, with the primary goal of having MV Realty’s liens, which bound 9,303 Florida homeowners, terminated from the public record. In February 2025, the court found MV Realty’s actions unconscionable and ordered that MV Realty terminate all Florida liens. In the final resolution of this case, the court entered two Consent Judgments against MV Realty and its principals, providing the following relief: $18 million suspended judgment against MV Realty, designated as $6 million in disgorgement for ill-gotten gains, $10 million in civil penalties, and $2 million in attorneys’ fees and costs;

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: $3 million in suspended penalties against MV Realty’s principals; $3 million payment required by MV Realty due by June 30, 2026; An injunction against any efforts to collect any monies from consumers related to the unconscionable Homeowner Benefit Agreement; Termination of all recordings in the public record related to Homeowner Benefit Agreements and the associated Memoranda; 10-year injunction against MV Realty’s principals related to conducting certain consumer-facing real estate activities; 10-year injunction against MV Realty’s principals creating or offering any class of assets secured by residential real property in Florida; and

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Secures Judgment Against MV Realty for Scamming Florida Homeowners | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: 10-year injunction against creating, operating, managing, or controlling any business that engages in consumer-facing telemarketing in Florida. Special Counsel Ellen Lyons served as lead counsel on the matter, along with Consumer Protection Division Deputy Director Sasha Funk Granai, Senior Counsel Sean Saval, and Special Counsel Diane Marger Moore. To view the Final Judgments filed in the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit, click here  and here .

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Issues Civil Subpoena to FICO for Alleged Anticompetitive Practices Harming Florida Consumers | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: “Floridians deserve fair access to credit—not a system controlled by one company that repeatedly jacks up prices and blocks competition,” said Attorney General James Uthmeier . “These skyrocketing costs are passed directly to consumers, making it harder for families to buy homes, finance cars, and secure essential services. My office will not tolerate monopoly abuse that harms Florida families.” FICO issues approximately 27 million credit scores daily and its scores are used in over 90% of U.S. lending decisions. The company’s practices fundamentally shape how Floridians purchase homes and cars and access essential services including banking, insurance, telecom, and utilities.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Issues Civil Subpoena to FICO for Alleged Anticompetitive Practices Harming Florida Consumers | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: For decades, FICO has maintained a monopoly in the business-to-business credit scoring market. Recent years have seen dramatic price increases—from under $1 per score to as high as $10—along with allegations of predatory pricing, illegal product bundling, exclusionary contracts with the major credit bureaus, and efforts to impede competitors. The CID requires FICO to produce all documents previously provided in the ongoing federal antitrust litigation, as well as: Internal assessments of market share and competitive position versus other competitors;

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Issues Civil Subpoena to FICO for Alleged Anticompetitive Practices Harming Florida Consumers | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: License agreements and contracts with the major credit bureaus, including negotiations over royalty rates, pricing tiers, and any “no equivalent products” clauses; Documents relating to communications with the credit bureaus about competitors; and All pricing histories and changes for FICO scoring products. The CID also includes questions on FICO’s competitors, antitrust compliance personnel and training, and internal antitrust reviews. This action reinforces Attorney General Uthmeier’s commitment to enforcing Florida’s antitrust laws, promoting competition, and protecting consumers from corporate practices that inflate costs and limit choice in markets critical to everyday life

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. —Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit against Evolve Construction, LLC, Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc., and six principals and officers, alleging the companies and individuals used unfair, deceptive, and unconscionable practices to prey on Florida consumers who needed residential roof repair, roof replacement, and water and mold remediation after Hurricanes Ian and Milton.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: “These companies knocked on doors after the storms, promised fast repairs, took insurance money, and left Florida families with unfinished homes and liens on their property,” said Attorney General James Uthmeier . “More than 60 percent of the consumers who complained to our office are seniors. The fraudsters should expect to be held accountable.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: “Our investigations and administrative prosecutions resulted in 12 final orders against Ahmed Darkawi, the loss of his license, and an opportunity for affected homeowners to help recover funds they lost,” said Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation Secretary Melanie S. Griffin . “We will continue working with Attorney General Uthmeier and our partners to pursue every action available under Florida law to prevent future victims, protect consumers, and safeguard the integrity of Florida’s construction industry.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: “Everybody has heard of storm chasers, but most homeowners have not heard of storm scammers,” said William Webb, Chairman of the Florida Home Builder’s Association . “These are the type of people that come in right after the storm claiming to be a contractor to help you out whether it’s your roof or other items that need attention. These scammers are out to take advantage of our uninformed homeowners that are already under duress from the storm. Don’t become a victim.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: The complaint, filed in the Twentieth Judicial Circuit in Lee County, alleges that the corporate defendants and the individual defendants operated as a common enterprise. At least 80 consumers from Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota, Hillsborough, Polk, Osceola, Manatee, Volusia, St. Lucie, St. Johns, and Broward Counties have filed complaints with the Attorney General’s Office. More than 60 percent of those consumers are seniors. Consumers alleged paying more than $1 million for work they did not receive as promised.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: Many insurance payments ranged from $5,000 to $80,000 per property, and the complaint alleges the defendants often collected those funds in full while leaving work unfinished or never started.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: According to the complaint, the defendants solicited homeowners in their homes immediately after the storms, misrepresenting the quality and scope of the work and how quickly repairs would begin and be completed. Sales representatives who were not licensed contractors offered “free” roof inspections and held themselves out as “experts.” The complaint alleges those representatives never held the home-solicitation sale permits required by Florida law. They promised expedited permits, accelerated timelines, and the best possible insurance settlement—then, the State alleges, took consumers’ insurance benefits and failed to perform the work.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: The complaint further alleges that defendants required consumers to sign an unconscionable “Contingency Agreement” that failed to provide a good-faith itemized estimate of costs, omitted cancellation language required by Florida law, imposed an unlawful cancellation penalty recharacterized as “liquidated damages,” and functioned as an unlawful assignment of insurance benefits. When consumers tried to cancel or obtain refunds for work that was never performed, the defendants allegedly refused. Some consumers received only partial or poor-quality work that failed inspections and caused additional property damage.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: The complaint alleges the defendants threatened to place liens on homes—and in some cases recorded liens, including for inaccurate amounts, and pursued foreclosure—even when no work was performed and no materials were purchased. Defendants also sent representatives to consumers’ homes to collect payments, leaving some consumers feeling physically threatened. The corporate defendants are Evolve Construction, LLC, a Florida limited liability company organized in 2021 with its principal place of business in Naples, and Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc., a Florida corporation formed in 2023, also based in Naples. The individual defendants named in the complaint are:

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: Patrick Antoine  of Lee County, Florida, an authorized member of Evolve Construction, LLC and secretary of Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc.; Ahmed Darkawi  of Hennepin County, Minnesota, an original registered agent, authorized person, and former manager of Evolve Construction, LLC; Jarret Gross  of Martin County, Florida, an authorized member of Evolve Construction, LLC; Aleksandr Guldshtadt , also known as Alex Gold, of Los Angeles County, California, former CEO of Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc. and a former authorized member, registered agent, and manager of Evolve Construction, LLC; John Vincent  of Los Angeles County, California, manager of Evolve Construction, LLC; and

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: Jaser “Jay” Zaabri  of Los Angeles County, California, a manager of Evolve Construction, LLC and chief financial officer of Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc. The lawsuit brings two counts under the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act: one against the corporate defendants for unfair, deceptive, or unconscionable practices in the marketing, sale, and provision of residential construction and restoration services, and one against the individual defendants for their direct participation in, knowledge of, and ability to control those practices.

chunks.text: ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches | My Florida Legal ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches TALLAHASSEE, Fla.— Attorney General James Uthmeier activated Florida's Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias heads toward the Florida Panhandle. Isaias became a major hurricane Friday morning and is expected to make landfall tonight or early Saturday.

chunks.title: ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: "Protecting Floridians isn't a seasonal job, and this hotline ensures that there is a simple process to report unconscionable increases in prices," said Attorney General James Uthmeier . "Whether it's a storm, a scam, or a greedy corporation, our office will enforce the law." Under Florida's price gouging statute, section 501.160, Florida Statutes, it is unlawful during a declared state of emergency to charge unconscionable prices for essential commodities and services needed to prepare for or recover from the storm. These include food, water, ice, gasoline, lumber, equipment and hotel rooms.

chunks.title: ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: The law applies within the counties covered by Governor DeSantis's state of emergency : Baker, Bay, Calhoun, Citrus, Columbia, Dixie, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Levy, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Suwannee, Taylor, Wakulla, Walton and Washington. Violators face civil penalties of $1,000 per violation, up to $25,000 for multiple violations committed in a single 24-hour period. Criminal sanctions may also apply. Floridians who suspect price gouging can report it through MyFloridaLegal.com or by calling 1-866-9-NO-SCAM. For more information on price gouging, click here .

chunks.text: Blaise Ingoglia serves the citizens of the state of Florida as the state's Chief Financial Officer, State Fire Marshal, and member of the Florida Cabinet. He soon found success as a mortgage broker and later founded Hartland Homes, a homebuilding company dedicated to helping working families achieve the dream of homeownership.

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: Ingoglia’s interest in public service was sparked in 2007 when he noticed local governments “going wild” spending property tax dollars. chunks.title: About the CFO

chunks.text: CFO Blaise Ingoglia’s top priority is making Florida more affordable, with a focus on lowering property taxes and reducing insurance costs for hardworking families. chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: Florida's CFO serves as one of three constitutionally elected state executives of the Florida Cabinet, which comprises the Chief Financial Officer, the Attorney General, and the Commissioner of Agriculture and Consumer Services. Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Cabinet serve as a board of directors, or agency heads, governing such matters as the purchase of state lands; clemency matters; state bond, trust and fund management; veterans' affairs; state law enforcement administration; tax collection; power plant and transmission line sitings; and financial and insurance regulation for the state of Florida.

chunks.text: PORT ST. LUCIE, Fla.- Today, Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Blaise Ingoglia announced over $46 million in the St. Lucie County budget as “excessive, wasteful spending.” The General Fund Budget increased by 76.01% since Fiscal Year (FY) 2019-2020. CFO Ingoglia is calling upon St. Lucie County’s elected officials to offer significant property tax relief. Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia Announces Over $59 Million in Flagler County Budget as “Excessive, Wasteful Spending”

chunks.title: Press Releases
chunks.text: PALM COAST, Fla.- Today, Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia announced over $59 million in the Flagler County budget as “excessive, wasteful spending”. The county has the highest budget increase among the past fifteen local governments that have been reviewed by the Florida Agency for Fiscal Oversight (FAFO) with a 119.2% increase. CFO Ingoglia is recommending that Flagler County offer immediate property tax relief to the taxpayers. Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia Announces Over $39 Million in Citrus County Budget as “Excessive, Wasteful Spending”

chunks.title: Press Releases
chunks.text: LECANTO, Fla.- Today, Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Blaise Ingoglia announced that Citrus County is excessively and wastefully spending more than $39 million in their General Fund Budget. Over the past six years, the budget has increased by 72.8%. CFO Ingoglia is calling upon Citrus County’s elected officials to offer substantial property tax relief and eliminate wasteful spending in the upcoming budget process. chunks.title: CFO Blaise Ingoglia Demands Local Governments Comply with DOGE Review Without Imposing Bureaucratic Red Tape
chunks.text: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. – Today, Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Blaise Ingoglia sent a letter to all local governments being reviewed by Florida DOGE after receiving information that some government entities are trying to impose conditions and bureaucratic red tape on employees who are looking for waste, fraud, and abuse of taxpayer dollars. CFO Ingoglia is committed to fighting on behalf of taxpayers and he will not stand for interference in this process. The CFO stands on the side of accountability and transparency, and he possesses broad constitutional and statutory audit authority to ensure fiscal responsibility from those entrusted with state dollars.

chunks.title: CFO Blaise Ingoglia Demands Local Governments Comply with DOGE Review Without Imposing Bureaucratic Red Tape
chunks.text: For government entities that do not wish to comply, CFO Ingoglia has one message: “The CFO has subpoena power to gain access to these files. I am not afraid to use that power.” The full letter from CFO Ingoglia can be found here . Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and State Fire Marshal Blaise Ingoglia serves as the state’s top financial watchdog, a member of the Florida Cabinet, and the head of the Florida Department of Financial Services. As CFO, he oversees billions of dollars in state funds and is committed to protecting taxpayer dollars, strengthening Florida’s fiscal health, and delivering essential services that support the state’s excellent economy. chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO Accessibility for everyone. Powered by MDW Communications Affordability · Accountability · Anti-Corruption Annette Taddeo's affordability plan starts with the costs Florida families feel most: home insurance, property taxes, and power. As Florida's Chief Financial Officer, she will use the powers the office already has to grade every insurance company, mail back the money the state owes you, and audit every no-bid deal in Tallahassee.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Annette has run a small business for 30 years, creating jobs and meeting a payroll. As a mother and a business owner, she pays Florida's rising costs too. And she is not afraid to stand up to the old boys club in Tallahassee, or to anyone, in any party, to give Florida families the economic relief they deserve. Tallahassee is rigged, and you're paying for it. Florida needs a watchdog, not a lapdog. Grade every insurance company, publicly. Within her first 100 days, a report card on how fast each insurer answers claims, how often they delay or deny payment, how much of your premium goes to their own affiliates, and how financially sound they are. Naming names.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Real tax relief, with safeguards. A bigger homestead exemption, and a backstop for rural counties so a tax cut doesn't come back as a higher tax rate. Mail you the money the state owes you. Florida is holding billions in unclaimed funds. Annette's office will match the records and send you your check. Show up after the storm. Strike teams on the ground in hit communities within 3 to 5 days, helping families push stalled and lowballed claims. Post every contract. Audit every no-bid deal. Every state contract in the public FACTS database, as the law requires. No exceptions, no hiding.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Go after corruption at every level of government. Her office's sworn investigators will follow the money and refer corrupt officials for prosecution, in any party. No campaign ads on your dime. Annette will not use taxpayer money to run campaign ads. Blaise Ingoglia has spent more than $3.7 million in taxpayer money on ads right as Floridians start voting. The man who built FAFO to hunt for waste is spending your money on his own campaign. Read the fine print before you get the bill. From AI data center deals to your pension, Annette will follow the money. Every promise on this page is something the CFO's office can actually do. That's the difference between a promise and a slogan.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Affordability is the issue in this race. Here is how Annette will lower the costs Florida families can no longer keep up with. How would Annette Taddeo lower homeowners insurance costs? Annette Taddeo will publish a public report card grading every home insurance company in Florida, so you can see who pays claims and who stalls before you buy a policy. She will use her Cabinet vote to fight for lower rates and full transparency from companies that cry poor while hiding their profits. Florida homeowners pay about $8,292 a year for insurance, the highest in the nation (opens in a new tab) . For most families, the insurance bill now costs more than their property taxes.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Blaise Ingoglia, the appointed CFO who is supposed to be watching this industry, has taken at least a quarter million dollars in political contributions from insurance interests. He also voted for a $3 billion tax handout to insurance companies while they kept charging Floridians the highest rates in the nation. Publish the Insurance Company Report Card: how fast each company responds to claims, how often it delays or denies payment, how much it raises rates, how much of your premium it pays to its own affiliates, and how financially sound it is. Every company, by name.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Fight for full transparency on insurance company "affiliates," the sister companies insurers pay while claiming they are losing money here. The state's own hidden report found insurers claiming $432 million in losses while their affiliates earned $1.3 billion. (More below.) Use her Cabinet vote and the bully pulpit of the CFO's office to fight for lower rates, and demand answers when executives pay themselves millions while your premium climbs.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: The Department of Financial Services' consumer complaint records and Division of Consumer Services, the Office of Insurance Regulation's public company filings, and the CFO's seat on the Financial Services Commission, which oversees the Office of Insurance Regulation. The first report card published within her first 100 days in office, and updated every year, with every company named. What did Florida's secret insurance report find?

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Annette fought on the Senate Banking and Insurance Committee for the state to fund a study on insurance company "affiliates," only for the government to keep the report hidden for four years. It found insurers claiming losses while seeking rate increases, as their sister companies made big profits from Floridians’ premiums. Annette Taddeo will put affiliate payments on her insurance report card and use her Cabinet vote to fight for the reforms Tallahassee keeps killing.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: In 2022, the Office of Insurance Regulation paid a consultant about $150,000 to study the fees insurers pay their own affiliates, sister companies with the same owners that handle claims, underwriting, and other services. The report was never released. When the Orlando Sentinel and South Florida Sun Sentinel obtained it through a public records request, the Florida Senate demanded they destroy it (opens in a new tab) and warned of "civil or criminal legal implications."

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: The newspapers published it anyway. Across 53 companies from 2017 to 2019, insurers claimed $432 million in losses (opens in a new tab) while paying fees to affiliates that earned $1.3 billion in net income. The consultant found 20 companies paying their affiliates at rates presumed not to be "fair and reasonable," the standard in Florida law. At least 17 reported losses while paying their affiliates more than they said they lost.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: It hasn't stopped. In 2025, key Florida insurers were still paying affiliates 20 to 35 percent of premiums, the same range the report found. This year the Florida House voted 106 to 3 to give regulators more power over affiliate payments. The bill died in the Senate. State regulators now call the report flawed and outdated, but they won't say what is wrong with it. And the insurers named in it dispute its findings. Floridians paid for this report. They deserve the full picture. Blaise Ingoglia holds a vote on the Financial Services Commission, which oversees the Office of Insurance Regulation. He has said nothing.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Show you where your premium goes. Annette's insurance report card will show what share of each company's premium goes to its own affiliates, drawn from the companies' public financial filings. Use her Cabinet vote to push for an updated, independent audit of affiliate payments, the one the House promised and then dropped, and to demand the results be made public. Fight for the affiliate reform the House passed 106 to 3: a clear legal definition of "fair and reasonable" and full disclosure to regulators of what affiliates are paid. Oppose every effort to hide reports the public paid for. Your premiums, your tax dollars, your right to know.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: The CFO's seat on the Financial Services Commission, which oversees the Office of Insurance Regulation and appoints the Insurance Commissioner; the Department of Financial Services' consumer information role; and the bully pulpit. New affiliate rules need the Legislature, and Annette will fight for them. Affiliate payments listed for every company on the first insurance report card, within her first 100 days. Where does Annette Taddeo stand on property taxes and Amendment 3?

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Annette Taddeo is all in on cutting taxes for Florida homeowners, and she supports a bigger homestead exemption . But Amendment 3 has no safeguards. It could bankrupt some of Florida's rural counties, and with nothing to stop local tax rates from going back up, many families could end up paying more, not less. That's why Annette is going after the biggest bill on your house first: insurance. Amendment 3 raises the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. State economists estimate (opens in a new tab) it would take about $12 billion a year out of local budgets. The amendment does not say how any of that gets replaced.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: The hardest hit are Florida's 29 fiscally constrained rural counties, which could lose 20 to 33 percent of their yearly revenue, according to the Florida Association of Counties (opens in a new tab) . These are small counties with few businesses to share the load. Property taxes pay for their sheriffs, their firefighters, and their ambulances.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: And there is nothing in it to keep your taxes from going back up. Local governments still set their own tax rates every year, and the amendment does not limit them (opens in a new tab) . When the money has to come from somewhere, it comes from higher rates on renters, small businesses, and everything else that is still taxed. Many families could end up paying more .

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Even Republican sheriffs and Firefighters are sounding the alarm. Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd (opens in a new tab) has urged voters to reject Amendment 3 and demand a plan that keeps public safety funded. The Governor now says "help for rural" (opens in a new tab) counties is coming if it passes. A promise is not a safeguard. It isn't written into the amendment. Here is the math that matters most. The average Florida homeowner pays about $8,292 a year for insurance, the highest in the nation, and far more than the typical property tax bill. If you want to put real money back in families' pockets, start with the biggest bill.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Cut taxes the right way. Annette supports raising the homestead exemption and real property tax relief, paid for honestly, with safeguards so the savings don't disappear into higher local rates and new fees. Stand with rural Florida. Annette will fight for any tax relief to come with a guaranteed backstop for fiscally constrained counties, so no community has to choose between a tax cut and a sheriff's deputy. Go after the biggest bill first. The insurance company report card (opens in a new tab) , the fight over hidden affiliate profits, and her Cabinet vote for lower rates all target the cost that is squeezing Florida homeowners hardest.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Find the money in Tallahassee first. Before anyone asks your county to cut firefighters, Annette will use the CFO's audit authority to go after the waste, no-bid contracts, and insider deals in state spending. Tell you the truth about your tax bill. If Amendment 3 passes, her office will track and publish, county by county, what happens to local budgets and tax rates, so you can see whether your tax cut was real.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Tax law is written by the Legislature and the voters, and the CFO does not set tax rates. What the CFO does have: audit authority over state spending, the state's checkbook and financial reporting, a Cabinet vote, and the bully pulpit of a statewide office. Annette will use all of them. A public, county-by-county report on local budgets and tax rates after Amendment 3, and an insurance report card in your hands within her first 100 days. Annette is for cutting your taxes. She is against a plan that defunds police and fire instead. How would Annette Taddeo fix Citizens Insurance?

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Annette Taddeo will appoint Citizens board members who answer to policyholders, not the insurance industry. The CFO directly appoints members of the Citizens Board of Governors, and Annette will use every seat she controls to put consumer champions at the table. More than 1.2 million Florida families rely on Citizens, the state-backed insurer, and every Florida policyholder is on the hook if it runs short. Families are being pushed off Citizens into private companies through "depopulation" deals. The executives of one company taking those policies collected nearly $38 million in compensation in a single year, disclosed in their own filing to Wall Street, while premiums kept climbing.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Appoint Citizens board members who answer to policyholders. Use her seat on the Financial Services Commission, which approves Citizens' plan of operation and appoints its independent Inspector General, to demand that depopulation serves families, not takeout companies. Fight for depopulation transparency: before any family is moved off Citizens, a clear, honest, side-by-side comparison of what they will pay and what coverage they will get. Direct appointment power over the Citizens Board of Governors, and the CFO's seat on the Financial Services Commission. Annette will publish the background of every Citizens board member she appoints, so you can see who they answer to.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: What will Annette Taddeo do after a hurricane? Annette Taddeo will send storm strike teams from the Department of Financial Services into hit communities within 3 to 5 days of a storm, in person, helping families push stalled and lowballed claims. No new law required. The trauma of a hurricane isn't just the premium. It's the slow-walked, lowballed claim that comes after, when families wait months for a check while living in a gutted house. Right now, when your insurer stalls, you're on your own. Deploy storm strike teams from the Division of Consumer Services into hit communities within 3 to 5 days of landfall.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Turn the state's insurance helpline into a unit with teeth: when a carrier lowballs or denies, her office will demand answers, escalate to investigators, and refer bad actors for enforcement. Expand the state's property insurance mediation program so families can fight a lowball offer without hiring a lawyer. Existing divisions of the CFO's own department: Consumer Services, the insurance fraud investigators, and the state mediation program. Given a mission and a deadline. Strike teams on the ground within 3 to 5 days of landfall, and a public report after every storm on how many claims her office helped move.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Annette Taddeo will flip the system. Instead of making you hunt for your money on a website, her office will match state records to current addresses and mail you your check. Her opponent calls your money abandoned. Annette will mail it back to you. The State of Florida is sitting on billions of dollars that belong to Florida families: dormant bank accounts, uncashed checks, forgotten insurance payouts. Roughly one in five Floridians has money waiting.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: This year, Tallahassee quietly changed the law to stop calling it your "unclaimed" money and start calling it "abandoned" property. You didn't abandon anything. The bank lost your address. A relative passed away. A check went to an old apartment. When a Florida couple went to federal court over their own $26.24 refund, the state argued they had walked away from it. The court rejected that argument. So Tallahassee changed the words in the law instead. Call your money what it is: yours. Not abandoned. Not the state's. Proactively match records to current addresses and mail you your check. Put seniors, veterans, and the families owed the most first in line for automatic returns.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: The unclaimed property program is run by the CFO's own department. No waiting on the Legislature. A public report every quarter on how much money went back into Floridians' pockets. How would Annette Taddeo help families afford a home? Annette Taddeo will fight for more down payment help and mortgage credit certificates for first-time buyers, using her Cabinet vote and audit authority over the Florida Housing Finance Corporation. She wants your kids to be able to afford to stay. Young families are being priced out of the state they grew up in, and Tallahassee has treated the housing crisis as someone else's problem.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Fight for expanded down payment assistance and mortgage credit certificates for first-time buyers. Champion homebuyer savings accounts that help working families build a down payment faster, modeled on programs already working in other states. Fight for rent payment reporting so renters who pay on time every month build the credit they deserve. Her Cabinet vote and audit authority over the Florida Housing Finance Corporation. New savings accounts and rent reporting need the Legislature, and Annette will use the bully pulpit to get them there. Annette will publish each year how much home buying help actually reached Florida families, and where. Will AI data centers raise my power bill?

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: They could, and Annette Taddeo won't wait to find out. She supports a moratorium (opens in a new tab) on new large-scale AI data centers until Florida has real, enforceable safeguards for ratepayers, water, and communities.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Massive AI data centers are coming to Florida, demanding enormous amounts of electricity and water. Tallahassee passed a law this year it said would shield ratepayers. Then Florida's biggest utility told Wall Street what the law really is: a profit engine. On its earnings call, FPL's parent company projected roughly $2 billion in guaranteed-return investment for every gigawatt of data center demand, and raised its forecast to 8 gigawatts by 2032 (opens in a new tab) . That is roughly $16 billion. The law's safeguards for you? Optional, at the discretion of a commission appointed by the Governor.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Energy companies have given Blaise Ingoglia over one hundred thousand dollars in political support while currently promoting the construction of massive hyperscale data centers across the state of Florida that will drive up utility costs for Florida families. Support a statewide moratorium on new large-scale AI data centers until Florida has enforceable safeguards for ratepayers, water, and communities. Use the CFO's audit authority to check the receipts and expose any cost-shifting that lands data center infrastructure on Florida families' bills.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Fight for full transparency on every data center deal. If a project needs your water and your power grid, you have a right to know who is behind it before it is approved. The CFO's audit authority and the bully pulpit. A moratorium needs action by the Legislature, and Annette will fight for it. Annette will publish what her audits find about who is really paying for data center infrastructure. Accountability means someone is watching your money. Right now with Blaise Ingoglia, no one is.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Florida law is clear: after one year, every dollar spent and every contract signed under an emergency must be audited, and every contract must be posted in the public FACTS database. Neither has happened. Annette Taddeo will audit Florida's emergency spending, starting with the $1.2 billion spent on Alligator Alcatraz, and publish what she finds in plain language.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Florida drained its Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund to under $7 million during hurricane and brush fire season, after roughly $890 million in spending. More than a billion dollars went out the door with no competitive bids and no independent audit. Meanwhile Blaise Ingoglia looked the other way and received a $100,000 check to his political committee from CDR Enterprises, the largest vendor for Alligator Alcatraz.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Florida Statutes require it (opens in a new tab) . Once a state of emergency lasts more than a year, all of its spending must be audited, and updated every year. Every contract signed to support the emergency, including the no-bid deals, must be posted in FACTS, the state's public contract database. Florida's immigration emergency has run for years. The audit hasn't happened, and hundreds of millions in contracts are still missing from FACTS.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Blaise Ingoglia built an audit operation, which he named FAFO, to go after county governments across the state. But he won't look at a single dollar the Governor spent on Alligator Alcatraz. Asked about it, his office said it had “ full confidence in the Trump Administration's financial review (opens in a new tab) .” That's not fiscal oversight. That's covering for the man who appointed him. Use the CFO's audit authority under Florida law to audit emergency spending, starting with Alligator Alcatraz and every no-bid deal behind it. Get every emergency contract posted in FACTS, as the law requires. The database is run by the CFO's own department. Refer anything improper to law enforcement.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Track every dollar of federal reimbursement Florida is eligible for and report on what has actually come back. Florida is eligible for up to $608 million from FEMA. So far, about $58 million has been reimbursed. Audit waste wherever it is, in any city, any county, and any state agency, no matter which party is in charge. Florida Statutes give the CFO the power to audit state accounts and refer anything improper to law enforcement (Section 17.04). The FACTS database, where every emergency contract must be posted, is run by the CFO's own department. Audit findings published in plain language, every emergency contract searchable in FACTS, and a quarterly public report on federal reimbursements.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: “Blaise Ingoglia is wrong. Auditing how state money is spent is the job. Florida Statutes give the CFO the power to audit state accounts and refer anything improper to law enforcement. He built FAFO to audit county governments across the state. But he won't look at a single dollar the governor spent on Alligator Alcatraz. That's not fiscal oversight. That's covering for the man who appointed him. The law is clear. After one year, every dollar spent and every contract signed under this emergency must be audited, and every contract must be posted in FACTS. That includes the no-bid deals. Neither has happened.”

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Yes. Annette Taddeo will apply one standard to every level of government, in any party. Blaise Ingoglia aimed his audits almost entirely at Democratic-led cities and counties while ignoring more than a billion dollars in documented waste at the state level. Florida's government spends over $100 billion a year, and for years the CFO has looked the other way because politicians in Tallahassee cover for each other and the donors who get no-bid contracts and tax handouts. That is not oversight. That is selective enforcement. Apply one standard of fiscal oversight to every level of government, regardless of party.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Start where the money is: the state contracts and emergency spending Blaise Ingoglia refuses to examine. Publish audit findings in plain language so every Floridian can follow the money. The CFO audits the state's payments and has audit authority across state government under Florida Statutes. Every audit Annette's office completes, state or local, published in one public place. A watchdog that only bites the other party's ankles is not a watchdog. It's a political weapon, and taxpayers are the ones getting bitten. How would Annette Taddeo fight HOA and condo fraud?

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: She already has. Annette Taddeo helped bring to justice one of the largest HOA frauds in American history, at the Hammocks in her Senate district. As CFO, she will put the state's sworn fraud investigators to work on HOA and condo theft statewide. Millions of Floridians live under HOAs and condo associations, and too many have watched their fees climb while board insiders treat community funds like a personal bank account. When theft happens, homeowners are told to hire a lawyer and hope. Put the Department of Financial Services' sworn fraud investigators to work on HOA and condo association theft, following the money and referring cases for prosecution.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Fight for real financial transparency and reserve reporting standards so families can see where their money goes before it disappears. Stand with homeowners fighting association insurance abuses, using the CFO's consumer role to help residents get answers from carriers. The Department of Financial Services' sworn law enforcement investigators and the CFO's authority to refer cases for prosecution. A public count of the HOA and condo fraud cases her office opens and refers for prosecution.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: The Hammocks is the largest HOA in Florida, home to roughly 18,000 residents. Annette spent years helping homeowners gather records and find the courage to speak to the State Attorney's office. People were threatened. She did not back down. The result: guilty pleas in an $11 million theft, the longest prison sentence ever given to an HOA president in the country, and a new state law for homeowners. Most candidates have talking points on HOA fraud. Annette has a record.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Annette Taddeo will keep politics out of your pension. She will use her seat as a trustee of the State Board of Administration to fight for one standard for the Florida Retirement System: the best returns for the people who earned them. Not the politics of the left or the right. The Florida Retirement System holds the pensions of teachers, police officers, firefighters, nurses, and public workers across the state. That money has one job: to be there when they retire.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: In recent years, politicians have used the state's investment decisions to make political statements and win headlines, instead of focusing on returns. Every investment decision made for politics instead of performance puts retirees' money at risk. Keep politics out of investment decisions, from any direction. Every investment judged on risk and return, never on a politician's agenda, left or right. Hold the board to its legal duty. State pension trustees are required to act solely in the interest of the retirees and workers who own this money. Annette will hold every vote to that standard.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO
chunks.text: Fight for full transparency on investment fees and performance, so retirees can see exactly how their money is managed and what it costs them. Bring 30 years of making payroll to the job, and treat your retirement with the seriousness it deserves. One of three trustee votes on the State Board of Administration, alongside the Governor and the Attorney General. Decisions take a majority, so Annette will use her vote and her voice. Annette will explain every major vote she casts on the State Board of Administration, in plain language, so you know how your retirement is being managed.

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO

chunks.title: The Issues — Annette Taddeo for Florida CFO

chunks.text: Wilton Has Delivered Key Investments in Florida’s Environment A lot of folks talk about the need for critical investments in Florida’s environment, but Wilton has actually done the work. chunks.title: Issues: David Jolly’s Policy Positions for Florida

A state catastrophic fund that removes natural disaster risk from the private insurance market would dramatically reduce property and car insurance rates, restoring affordability and price stability for millions of Floridians. Allowing condominium associations and owners access to a no-interest state-backed loan program would likewise address the crushing financial burden of generational condominium repairs.

chunks.title: Issues: David Jolly’s Policy Positions for Florida

Private schools that accept vouchers should be required to provide the same specialized services public schools provide and not charge additional tuition. The voucher program should be means-tested to ensure funding is provided for families with demonstrated economic need.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor David Jolly's Plan to Cut Florida Homeowners Insurance by 60 to 70 Percent Floridians pay the highest home insurance prices in America because every family is made to pay a private insurer to carry hurricane risk. Jolly's proposal moves that risk into one strong, state-backed fund. Here is how it works, what it costs, and what it saves.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: David Jolly's plan creates a state-backed hurricane fund to carry hurricane and wind risk, which makes up 60 to 70 percent of Florida homeowners insurance bills. Private insurers would no longer price hurricane risk into policies, cutting costs by an estimated 64 percent (about $4,500 a year for a $300,000 home, dropping from $7,136 to $2,557). The fund is paid for by making insurance companies pay taxes they currently avoid and other sources that do not burden homeowners, with coverage starting only after the fund is financially sound and backed by reinsurance. What hurricane risk costs a Florida family today

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: Insure.com's Florida home insurance calculator, for a $300,000 home with a $1,000 deductible: the average policy priced with hurricane risk, and the same policy priced without it. Floridians are paying the highest home insurance prices in America, and the private market has collapsed. Company after company has pulled out of the state or gone under, and the ones that remain price every policy for the worst storm they can imagine, because in Florida the worst storm is not hypothetical.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: The main reason a Florida policy costs so much more than one in Georgia or Ohio is one line on the bill: hurricane and wind. That single risk can be 60 to 70 percent of what a family pays. Every other part of a homeowners policy—fire, theft, liability, a burst pipe—is priced roughly the way it is priced anywhere else. Instead of forcing every Florida family to pay a private insurer to take on that enormous hurricane risk, Jolly's proposal does four things, in order. Florida creates one strong, state-backed hurricane fund. One fund, for the whole state, carrying hurricane and wind risk for Florida homes.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: The fund is built to a financially sound level and buys backup insurance for catastrophic storms. Coverage does not start until enough money is set aside and reinsurance for the biggest storms is in place. The fund is built first; it does not borrow against a storm that has not happened. The fund is paid for without putting the burden back on homeowners. Insurance companies would start paying the taxes they currently avoid. Other sources that do not put a burden on homeowners, such as a fee on real estate transactions or existing tourist taxes, are on the table. The Legislature writes the specific funding policy. How the fund is paid for, in detail.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: Private insurers no longer have to price hurricane risk into your policy. That is where the 60 to 70 percent savings comes from. The rest of your policy stays private, competitive, and priced the way policies are in other states. Florida already has a state catastrophic fund. The Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund was created in a special legislative session in November 1993, after Hurricane Andrew, and it has been run and expanded by Republican legislatures for three decades. Right now, that fund only reimburses insurance companies for a share of their hurricane losses. It is a bailout for insurers.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: David Jolly's plan takes a structure Florida has already proven and directs it to the people who actually pay the bills. Does Florida already have a hurricane catastrophe fund? The fund is rolled out responsibly. Coverage becomes available only after a fiscally sound amount of money is set aside and backup reinsurance is in place. The Legislature is involved in creating the specific policies, including the funding. And in the end, the costs will be lower for Floridians, or we won't do it. Simple as that.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: Byron Donalds is running ads claiming this proposal creates a "$1,000 hurricane tax." It does not. The ad's two "sources" are a legislative feasibility study that did not look at Jolly's proposal and an opinion blog post. When reporters asked Donalds about the number, he didn't give them a source; instead, he referred to an entirely different, unrelated law. We answer the claim, and the study, on their own pages: Does David Jolly want a $1,000 hurricane tax? What is the study Byron Donalds cites in his hurricane tax ad? Will David Jolly's catastrophe fund raise costs for Floridians? What is Byron Donalds' plan to lower insurance costs?

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: "Losing campaigns lie. What Byron is doing is using fear to try to stop progress." David Jolly, September 14, 2026. Q. How much would David Jolly's plan save on homeowners insurance? Hurricane and wind risk can be 60 to 70 percent of a Florida homeowners bill. Based on Insure.com's Florida home insurance calculator, a $300,000 home with a $1,000 deductible averages $7,136 a year when the policy is priced with hurricane risk and $2,557 when it is not. That is a 64 percent difference, about $4,500 a year. Q. Who pays for the state catastrophe fund?

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: Not homeowners. The plan funds it by making insurance companies pay the taxes they currently avoid, and through other sources that do not put the burden back on homeowners, such as a fee on real estate transactions or existing tourist taxes. The Legislature writes the specific funding policy. Only after the fund reaches a fiscally sound level and backup reinsurance for catastrophic storms is in place. The fund is built first, then it covers people. Q. Does Florida already have something like this?

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor
chunks.text: Yes. The Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund has existed since 1993. Today it reimburses insurance companies for a share of their hurricane losses; it does not cover homeowners directly. The plan applies a structure Florida has already proven to the people who pay the bills. Q. Is there a $1,000 hurricane tax in the plan? No. There is no $1,000 fee, tax or assessment on homeowners in the plan. The claim comes from a Byron Donalds ad whose sources are a legislative feasibility study of a different proposal and an opinion blog post. The full answer is at /homeowners-insurance/hurricane-tax/.

chunks.title: Florida Homeowners Insurance Plan: David Jolly for Governor

The premium comparison is from Insure.com's Florida homeowners insurance calculator for a $300,000 dwelling with a $1,000 deductible, comparing the policy priced with a hurricane deductible against the standard policy. The history of the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund is from the State Board of Administration , which runs it. David Jolly's remarks are from his September 14, 2026 video press conference and from Florida Phoenix . This page was last reviewed on September 15, 2026 and is re-verified as the story develops.
